summary: Generate MO files addon generates incorrect MO file from monolingual PO file
description:
**Describe the bug**
When using the `Generate MO files` addon, the resulting MO files when creating from monolingual PO files are incorrect. For the `msgid`, only the first character from the ID is taken and used. Also, every entry has a `msgid_plural` property, even though the original file does not have them. Moreover, the `msgstr` is array based, with only one entry (not sure if this last one is a problem).

I've included a snippet of the original `.po` file and the resulting `.mo` at the bottom of this issue.

This issue is very much related to [this issue](https://github.com/WeblateOrg/weblate/issues/2658). We had that problem as well, and were eager to use the fix for the 3.6 version, but now we're encountering this problem. Though, the resulting problems in the MO files are different, hence creating a new issue instead of commenting on the linked one.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior (copied from the linked issue, because the steps are the same):
1. Add a component which uses monolingual PO files
2. Add the MO addon
3. Translate some files
4. Commit the changes
5. Check the generated MO file with a gettext tool, for example `msgunfmt` on the command line.

**Expected behavior**
The resulting MO structure from the `msgunfmt` command should be identical (or functionally identical) to the original PO file.

**Example file**

Snippet from the PO file:
```
msgid "action.cancel.text"
msgstr "cancel"

msgid "action.confirm.text"
msgstr "confirm"
```

Snippet from the `msgunfmt` result of the MO file (with the same fields):
```
msgid "a"
msgid_plural "c"
msgstr[0] "cancel"

msgid "a"
msgid_plural "c"
msgstr[0] "confirm"
```

description:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

* Originally observed when preparing Docker container upgrade to Debian buster, see https://github.com/WeblateOrg/docker/pull/152.

* possible workaround https://github.com/tesseract-ocr/tesseract/issues/1670#issuecomment-431560537

summary: Weblate is unable to deal with private-use subtags
description:
**Describe the bug**
Per RFC 4646 and RFC 4647 now collectively BCP 47 (https://www.w3.org/International/articles/language-tags/ , http://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/bcp/bcp47.txt) private-use subtags are valid language codes. For example `en-US-x-twain` or `de-x-a123` is valid. In our case we use this to translate customer specific strings in our application where `twain` or `a123` is the customer. We would like to manage this in weblate however if we import xliff files with such tags weblate will incorrectly recognise the language code.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Create a language in weblate `de-x-a123`
2. Add component with xliff file called comp.de-x-a123.xlf (source-language="de" target-language="de-x-a123")
3. Weblate will auto-create new a language withe code `de_X-G` instead of `de-x-a123`

**Expected behavior**
Languages such as `de-x-a123` are correctly detected

**Server configuration and status**

```

 * Python 2.7.13
 * Django 1.11.17
```

summary: Make Weblate compliant with Google API Policy

Since November 2018, all apps need to get approval by Google of the OAuth consent screen. So trying to comply with this policy, I have installed Legal module, wrote a simple Privacy Policy. But Google has rejected my request with the following message:

> 1. Privacy Policy
> 
> [Google API Service:User Data Policy](https://developers.google.com/terms/api-services-user-data-policy) requires the following:
> 
> Your Privacy policy must be visible to users, hosted within the domain of your website, and linked to the OAuth consent screen on [Google API Console](https://console.developers.google.com/).
> 
> Your privacy policy and in-product privacy notifications must thoroughly disclose the manner in which your application accesses, uses, stores, or shares Google user data. Your use of Google user data must be limited to the practices explicitly disclosed in your published privacy policy.

> 
> The Google sign-in button on your project's homepage URL is not compliant with the Google sign-in branding guidelines. Please update the Google sign-in button on your website according to [Google sign-in branding guidelines](https://developers.google.com/identity/branding-guidelines#top_of_page).

As I understand from this message, link to Privacy Policy should be direct. Currently, it's not visible unless you click Legal.

Here are my thoughts what's needed to be done:
1. Make Legal module installed by default.

4. Make Google Sign In button compliant with their branding guidelines.

summary: [XLIFF] Editing source monolingual file with only Source should only update Source
description:
**Describe the bug**
Weblate lets you edit the source translation file. When editing a XLIFF that only uses Source strings in the base file, they're not updated correctly. In a monolingual XLIFF file, the `<target>` is redundant.

This is related to #2481.

For example:

```
<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?>
<xliff xmlns="urn:oasis:names:tc:xliff:document:1.2" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" version="1.2" xsi:schemaLocation="urn:oasis:names:tc:xliff:document:1.2 xliff-core-1.2-transitional.xsd">
  <file datatype="xml" source-language="en-US" target-language="en-US" original="Translation">
    <body>
      <group id="body">
        <trans-unit id="123456789" size-unit="char" translate="yes" xml:space="preserve" approved="yes">
          <source>Original String</source>
          <target>Original String</target>
        </trans-unit>
      </group>
    </body>
  </file>
</xliff>
```

**To Reproduce**
Use the following file as a "base" file, then edit or approve the translation:

```
<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?>
<xliff xmlns="urn:oasis:names:tc:xliff:document:1.2" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" version="1.2" xsi:schemaLocation="urn:oasis:names:tc:xliff:document:1.2 xliff-core-1.2-transitional.xsd">
  <file datatype="xml" source-language="en-US" target-language="en-US" original="Translation">
    <body>
      <group id="body">
        <trans-unit id="123456789" size-unit="char" translate="yes" xml:space="preserve">
          <source>Original String</source>
        </trans-unit>
      </group>
    </body>
  </file>
</xliff>
```

**Expected behavior**
- If the translation is edited, then the `<source>` element should be updated, instead a `<target>` element is created.
- If the translation is the same as the `<source>`, then no `<target>` element should be created. Source can remain as-is and it can be marked as Done,

**Additional context**
Interestingly, the "Group" element is maintained which is awesome. I assume this is because Weblate isn't regenerating the entire file but just making changes. This means no fix for "base" file edits will be required in #2482 (still required for translations though).

summary: Adding a language with an underscore to a component results in the created xliff to be invalid
description:
**Describe the bug**
When a new language is addd to a component that contains an underscore, the created xliff file will have as `target-language` the language with underscore. From my understanding an underscore is not permitted in the field `target-language` as the xliff spec (https://docs.oasis-open.org/xliff/v1.2/os/xliff-core-1.2-strict.xsd) defines the field as `<xsd:attribute name="target-language" type="xsd:language" use="optional"/>` where `xsd:language` is defined as `[a-zA-Z]{1,8}(-[a-zA-Z0-9]{1,8})*` (http://www.datypic.com/sc/xsd/t-xsd_language.html)

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Add a new language that contains an underscore to a component . i.e `en_US`
2. Resulting new xlf file will have `target-language="en_US"`

**Expected behavior**
I think the correct thing to do would be to replace the `_` with a `-` in the xlf file and leave the filename as `_`.

summary: URL_PREFIX is not used when commit_pending is invoked by cron task

"male/female"

Whenever I click the "Process" button in the Automatic Translation form, I would get a 404 Error because the following URL does not exist:

"http://<MY_TM_SERVER>/tmserver/en/fr/unit/**male/female**"

I guess the previous URL should instead be:

"http://<MY_TM_SERVER>/tmserver/en/fr/unit/**male%2Ffemale**"

With the slash encoded.

I'm guessing it could be fixed by changing the way the url is created in /usr/local/lib/python3.5/dist-packages/weblate/machinery/tmserver.py (method: download_translations), but I'm not really sure since I'm quite new to Python.

Thank you!

summary: Importing Joomla! INI files adds surrounding "_QQ_" on every string
description:
### Steps to reproduce
1. Create a language in the Joomla! INI format
2. Import an INI file

Sample:
```
COM_EXAMPLE_FOO="This is a test"
```

### Actual behaviour
The string is imported as
```
COM_EXAMPLE_FOO=""_QQ_"This is a test"_QQ_""
```

### Expected behaviour
The string should have been imported as
```
COM_EXAMPLE_FOO="This is a test"
```

### Server configuration
Output of `./manage.py list_versions`

```
 * Weblate 2.17
 * Python 2.7.12
 * Django 1.11.6
 * six 1.10.0

 * python-bidi 0.4.0
 * PyYAML 3.11
 * Mercurial 3.7.3
 * Database backends: django.db.backends.mysql
```

### Further notes

I think this happens because the import treats the surrounding double quotes as part of the string proper instead of file format markup. Unfortunately I don't speak enough Python to debug this.

I do speak plenty of PHP and have been a long time contributor to Joomla! itself, though. In that capacity I can tell you that Joomla! no longer uses `"_QQ_"` since around 2014. Instead, double quotes in strings are supposed to be escaped with a backslash i.e. `\"`. Example:
```
COM_EXAMPLE_TEST="This is a \"special\" string."
```
As a result the generated Joomla! INI strings should not use `"_QQ_"` but `\"`. If you need me to file another issue for this let me know.

summary: msgctxt in monolingual Gettext files
description:
When using msgctxt in monolingual Gettext files, it's not possible to upload the file as the identifier is contructed from msgid + msgctxt.

Most likely it doesn't make sense to mix msgctxt into identifier for the monolingual files.

Sample causing the problems:

```po
msgctxt "False/True|FTF_TRUE"
msgid "00423|00001"
msgstr "True"
```

As a workaround comments can be used instead of msgctxt:

```po
#. False/True|FTF_TRUE
msgid "00423|00001"
msgstr "True"
```

summary: invalid regular expression: invalid escape \ sequence
description:
### Steps to reproduce
I'm not sure how to reproduce, I think this happens when you have accented characters in the dictionary and you try to go to this URL: https://weblate.example.com/translate/myproject/myproject/de/?type=nottranslated. The [dictionary query](https://github.com/WeblateOrg/weblate/blob/weblate-2.17/weblate/trans/models/dictionary.py#L180) that gets built uses `re.escape` to escape the words, and as stated in the [Python docs](https://docs.python.org/3/library/re.html#re.escape):

> Escape all the characters in pattern except ASCII letters, numbers and '_'.

This means characters such as accented characters will be escaped as well and will cause the query to fail (with the error message from PostgreSQL "invalid regular expression: invalid escape \ sequence"). Looking at the [PostgreSQL docs](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/9.3/static/functions-matching.html) this seems indeed illegal:

> A \ followed by an alphanumeric character but not constituting a valid escape is illegal in AREs.

Executing this query produces an error from PostgreSQL. I guess the regular expression escaping shouldn't be done on Python's side but rather on the database side, since each database engine could have different escape rules.

The generated query looks like this:

```
SELECT "trans_dictionary"."id", "trans_dictionary"."project_id", "trans_dictionary"."language_id", "trans_dictionary"."source", "trans_dictionary"."target" FROM "trans_dictionary" WHERE ("trans_dictionary"."project_id" = 2 AND "trans_dictionary"."language_id" = 46 AND "trans_dictionary"."source"::text ~* '^(word\ 1|word\ with\ an\ accent\ \é)$') ORDER BY "trans_dictionary"."source" ASC;
```

[The following thread](https://www.postgresql.org/message-id/4F47C2D6.8000207%40gmail.com) on the PostgreSQL mailing list seems to refer to the same problem.

### Actual behaviour
The page fails with a 500 error.

### Expected behaviour
The page should display the current translations.

A row of "save" requests take a minute each:
```
[pid: 27173|app: 0|req: 14/57] xx.xx.xxx.xx () {68 vars in 1546 bytes} [Mon Jul 17 19:49:24 2017] POST /translate/fallout2-up/male/es/?type=check%3Aend_ellipsis&offset=5 => generated 0 bytes in 61222 msecs (HTTP/1.1 302) 6 headers in 411 bytes (1 switches on core 0)
```
In top, I see Mysql spike to 200% CPU for a moment, then uwsgi keeps at 90-100% for the whole minute. Mysql slow logs don't show anything over 1 sec. I also tried disabling Redis cache, that didn't help.

Looks like a timeout of some sort, but I'm not sure how to debug it.

summary: Weblate not outputing Android <plurals> fields properly, causing app crashes
description:
With Hebrew, the user interface shows One and Other as the options:
* https://hosted.weblate.org/translate/f-droid/f-droid/he/?checksum=&offset=0&q=details_last_update_weeks&search=substring&context=on&type=all&ignored=

But the _strings.xml_ then has One and Two filled out, then Many and Other blank:
```xml
<plurals name="details_last_update_weeks">
	<item quantity="one">עודכן לפני שבוע</item>
	<item quantity="two">עודכן לפני %1$d שבועות</item>
	<item quantity="many"></item>
	<item quantity="other"></item>
</plurals>
```

An empty Other string can cause crashes.  Especially because we remove blank strings, since they cause other problems.  Weblate should ensure that if any item of `<plurals>` has been translated, then `<item quantity="other">` must be translated.  Here's the Android source reference on the requirement for other:
https://android.googlesource.com/platform/frameworks/base/+/master/core/java/android/content/res/ResourcesImpl.java#268

summary: HTML source string starting with DOCTYPE does not trigger XML checks
description:
### Steps to reproduce
1. Have a source string that contains HTML content starting with a DOCTYPE declaration
2. Enter translation for that source string that contains broken XML/HTML
3. Save

### Actual behaviour
XMLValidityCheck did not detect the mistake

### Expected behaviour
The XML check should have noticed that the translation was invalid.

### Server configuration
 * Weblate weblate-2.10
 * Python 2.7.12+
 * Django 1.10.5
 * six 1.10.0
 * python-social-auth 0.2.21
 * Translate Toolkit 2.0.0rc2
 * Whoosh 2.7.4
 * defusedxml 0.4.1
 * Git 2.9.3
 * Pillow (PIL) 1.1.7
 * dateutil 2.6.0
 * lxml 3.7.2
 * django-crispy-forms 1.6.1
 * compressor 2.1
 * djangorestframework 3.5.3
 * pytz 2016.10
 * pyuca N/A
 * python-bidi 0.4.0
 * pyLibravatar N/A
 * PyYAML 3.12
 * Mercurial 4.0.2
 * Database backends: django.db.backends.postgresql_psycopg2

### Personal analysis
Weblate first checks whether the source string is valid XML. If it isn't, it is not even going to try validating the translation. Checking whether something is valid XML is done by surrounding the text with `<weblate></weblate>` tags.

This fails when the text starts with a DOCTYPE declaration. The SyntaxError that gets thrown, says something like this:
```
XML declaration allowed only at the start of the document, line 1, column 15 (line 1)
```
As Weblate did not consider the source string XML, then it won't even check the translation for valid XML.

Suggestion: Improve the parse_xml method in the BaseXMLCheck class. Somehow detect the DOCTYPE and maybe... strip it, or don't surround it with `<weblate></weblate>`?

I assume there might be a similar issue when XML starts with
```
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
```

summary: Other translations: 2.12 regression?
description:
Hello,

Looks like "Other translations" always features the **current unit** (tagged as **"This translation"**)

I feel this is a **2.12 regression** (well, kind of by design - cf. 88663cf524d82c0b9a50e2fb571e031ddb2f5951)

Looking a bit more into this commit, I feel we should just hide the output when the only returned item is the current translation - the current on-screen behaviour is a bit unsettling...

(When there are indeed items with same source & context in other components, then I agree it's useful to see the current unit right along the other ones i.e. you have a direct consistency check view) 

Also, gotta make sure that `others_count` works as expected.

On a separate note, do you think it might be useful to see (somewhere...) the "Other translations" but with same source and not necessarily same context - i.e. both intra-component and across components... ?

Thanks,

Marc

summary: Save button in profile>Subscriptions>Subscription Settings is broken
description:
### Steps to reproduce
1. Log in and navigate to your profile
2. select the Subscriptions tag
3. toggle one or more  subscription check box, remembering which you change.
4. click the save button in Subscription settings 
5. After the refresh, check that the changes made in step 3 are still displayed
6. Log in as a different user and trigger one of the events that you have (un)subscribed to in step 3

### Actual behaviour
In my case, the complete installation is new, so toggling is firstly a subscribe. 
in step 5 the check boxes are all unsubscribed - even those i checked!  The change was either not saved to the database, or not displayed correctly. Triggering an event that should have been subscribed to,   should have caused an e-mail to be sent, but no mail was sent. examining the database reveals that the events are all still set to false. eg for test user bart

```sql
select
   subscribe_any_translation,
   subscribe_new_string,
   subscribe_new_suggestion,
   subscribe_new_contributor,
   subscribe_new_comment,
   subscribe_merge_failure,
   subscribe_new_language,
   username
from
  accounts_profile,
  auth_user
where auth_user.id = accounts_profile.user_id
and   username='bart';
```

I get the folowing output even if I have tried to set all check boxes
```
 subscribe_any_translation | subscribe_new_string | subscribe_new_suggestion | subscribe_new_contributor | subscribe_new_comment | subscribe_merge_failure | subscribe_new_language | username
---------------------------+----------------------+--------------------------+---------------------------+-----------------------+-------------------------+------------------------+----------
 f                         | f                    | f                        | f                         | f                     | f                       | f                      | bart
(1 row)
```

Further investigation with a colleague  using Firefox's Inspector reveal that the save button is outside the form element to which it refers - moving the button inside the form using the inspector can make the button work.  

The save button is inside the div surrounding the subscriptions form, but **outside** that form, it is therefore inside the form that is created for Watched projects, Description and Subscription settings.

### Expected behaviour
The changes in step 3 are saved to the database, and can be seen in the refresh after the save and have an effect on the subsciriptions.  eg new subscription means new mail on that event is sent when another user   triggers  the event, unsubscribe means other user triggering an event send no mail.

Standard.

summary: Commit message stuck from previous translation entry, with no way to remove
description:
I have been using Hosted Weblate (F-Droid project) for quite some time, and encountered a problem: when I specified commit message and submit a string translation, this commit message will carry on to the next string translation form (considerably normal); but when I submitted this second string translation **with empty commit message**, the previous non-empty commit message will persistently carry on to the third string translation form; this is a problem since there is no way to change commit message back to empty one (it can only be changed to other non-empty messages).

The result is once the commit message has been set in the session, translator must manually clear the commit message before submitting _every subsequent translation_ that are not using commit message. When translator forgot to do it, wrong/nonsensical commit message would appear on the log, causing confusion to the software developer.

### Steps to reproduce

- Login to Hosted Weblate service <https://hosted.weblate.org/>.
- Visit F-Droid Hosted Weblate project <https://hosted.weblate.org/projects/f-droid/>
- Enter "F-Droid" component <https://hosted.weblate.org/projects/f-droid/f-droid/>
- Pick some random language.
- Go to "All strings".
- Submit first string translation with non-empty commit message.
- You will see that second string translation will show the previously-used commit message as default.
- Submit second string translation _with empty commit message_.
- You will see that third string translation would *still show the non-empty commit message from the first string* as default (instead of showing the expected empty commit message).

### Actual behaviour

Once the commit message in the translation form is cleared and the form is submitted, a form appeared for next string still have commit message field filled with the last non-empty commit message used in the sesion.

### Expected behaviour

Once the commit message in the translation form is cleared and the form is submitted, a form appeared for next string should have an **empty** commit message field.

### Workaround

Current workaround is to logout and re-login to clear the residual commit message every time the translator submitted string with commit message; simply exiting translation section/project and going back in again is not enough.

### Server configuration

Weblate: 2.10-dev <https://hosted.weblate.org/>
Hosted Weblate Project: F-Droid/F-Droid/Thai <https://hosted.weblate.org/translate/f-droid/f-droid/th/>

summary: Warn users & project owners against starting translations to deprecated codes
description:
There are a few language codes that, in general, should be avoided. This includes old Norwegian (`no`) and "Chinese" without script/region specifiers (`zh`). Under certain conditions, there are a few more language codes to avoid:
- "Chinese simplified" (`zh_Hans`) when a `zh_CN` translation exists. The opposite should apply as long as nobody is translating for `zh_SG`.
- "Chinese traditional" (`zh_Hant`) when either `zh_TW` or `zh_HK` exists.
- "Chinese simplified" (`zh_Hans`) and "Chinese traditional" (`zh_Hant`) in general as script-based division for Chinese is not a good idea. `Hant` is especially problematic as two major variants are written in that script.
- "English (United States)" when the source itself is in English. Only applies to users.

With that in mind, some warnings should be given to users when they try to use these deprecated language codes. `zh` is an especially great headache for me -- I always have to view the strings to figure out which script a translation is in. 
### Steps to reproduce
1. Open a project page, say, https://hosted.weblate.org/projects/wincompose/master/
2. Try to create a deprecated language. I tried with old Norwegian, so please delete that afterwards...
### Actual behaviour

summary: Automatic groups assignment does not work with LDAP authentication
description:
Automatic groups assignment does not seem to work properly when the user is created/authenticated through LDAP.
(NB: that's the only non-std authentication backend I've played with, not sure whether the issue is reproducible with other backends)
To reproduce the issue, create a non-trivial automatic groups assignment entry (unlike ^.*$ => Users), have an effective LDAP auth configured and login with a new (for Weblate) user.

Analysis: 
Probably (to be verified) the LDAP attribute mapping is performed after the post_save signal from User sender, so that email is basically unavailable (empty) in create_profile_callback.

A solution that seems to work for me (cf. diff below) is to re-do the Automatic groups assignment work upon another signal, namely populate_user from LDAPBackend.

```
--- a/ecccd210e57d4a9901e92af9832870af9fdf4d64:weblate/accounts/auth.py
+++ b/1690c137014861c66d3d220d41a874be90493df2:weblate/accounts/auth.py
@@ -19,8 +19,9 @@
 #

 import sys
+import re

-from django.contrib.auth.models import User, Permission
+from django.contrib.auth.models import User, Permission, Group
 from django.shortcuts import redirect
 from django.core.urlresolvers import reverse
 from django.db.models.signals import pre_save
@@ -28,12 +29,16 @@ from django.dispatch.dispatcher import receiver
 from django.utils.translation import ugettext as _
 from django.contrib.auth.backends import ModelBackend

+from django_auth_ldap.backend import populate_user
+from django_auth_ldap.backend import LDAPBackend
+
 import social.backends.email
 from social.exceptions import AuthMissingParameter

 from weblate.appsettings import ANONYMOUS_USER_NAME
 from weblate.trans import messages
 from weblate.trans.util import report_error
+from weblate.accounts.models import AutoGroup

 class EmailAuth(social.backends.email.EmailAuth):
@@ -125,3 +130,14 @@ def disable_anon_user_password_save(sender, *_kwargs):
     if (instance.username == ANONYMOUS_USER_NAME and
             instance.has_usable_password()):
         raise ValueError('Anonymous user can not have usable password!')
+
+@receiver(populate_user, sender=LDAPBackend)
+def auto_groups_upon_ldap(sender, *_kwargs):
-    # As the User's post_save django signal is apparently called before
-    # LDAP attribute mapping, it's necessary to perform the automatic groups
-    # assignment here too:
-    user = kwargs['user']
-    # Add user to automatic groups ()
-    for auto in AutoGroup.objects.all():
-        if re.match(auto.match, user.email):
-            user.groups.add(auto.group)
```

summary: [Android strings.xml] Weblate adds XML namespace in the wrong place, causing Gradle build to fail
description:
### Steps to reproduce
1. Create an Android project with a `tools:ignore` attribute on a string, like [this](https://github.com/vickychijwani/quill/blob/master/app/src/main/res/values/strings.xml#L34). Example:
   
   ``` xml
   <resources xmlns:tools="http://schemas.android.com/tools">
       <string name="string1" tools:ignore="PluralsCandidate">string1</string>
       <string name="string2">string2</string>
   </resources>
   ```
2. Translate the string via Weblate
3. Try to build the project with the translated strings file
### Actual behaviour

Weblate moves the `xmlns:tools="http://schemas.android.com/tools"` part to the string that uses the `tools` namespace, instead of attaching it to the root element `<resources>`.

``` xml
<resources>
      <string xmlns:tools="http://schemas.android.com/tools" name="string1" tools:ignore="PluralsCandidate">string1</string>
      <string name="string2">string2</string>
</resources>
```

This causes Gradle build to fail with this error:

```
Building 71% > :app:processDebugResources/home/.../values-ja.xml:2: AAPT: Error parsing XML: prefix must not be bound to one of the reserved namespace names
```

You can see a real failure of this sort here (Ctrl + F for "Error parsing XML"): https://circleci.com/gh/vickychijwani/quill/106
### Expected behaviour

The attribute `xmlns:tools="http://schemas.android.com/tools"` should be on the root `<resources>` element, not on the individual string.
### Server configuration

N/A (using Hosted Weblate)

summary: Java .properties strings defaulting to English - Weblate confused
description:
Hello there, first of all, thanks for a great piece of software! Now, my situation is this:
- `Strings.properties` - default strings, contain EN translation.
- `Strings_en.properties` - empty file, "marker" to show we have an EN translation.
- `Strings_fr.properties` - FR translation, some strings are missing - those default to the EN version.

My approach is based on the [SO question](http://stackoverflow.com/questions/36011759/resourcebundle-that-defaults-to-english) I posted a few days ago.

Weblate's config:
- File mask: `src/company/project/resources/Strings_*.properties`
- Monolingual base language file: `src/company/project/resources/Strings_en.properties`

Problem is, Weblate now thinks there are no strings (`Strings_en` is empty), so every other translation pretends to be 100% translated.

If I tell Weblate that the base file is `src/company/project/resources/Strings.properties` (as it actually is), it complaints **"There are more files for single language, please adjust the mask and use components for translating different resources."**.

In the end, Java's system of finding default strings requires me to have the `Strings.properties` in place, while Weblate is confused by this and wants an explicit `Strings_en.properties`. Is there a way out of this? Ideally I would like to avoid having to copy/paste or hard-link `Strings_en` to `Strings`...

Using Weblate 2.5-dev.

summary: Enabling GroupACL removes permission to add suggestions
description:
### Steps to reproduce
1. Precondition: Have "Suggestions" enabled for your components
2. Create a group "Translators" with permission to add/change translations and _suggestions_ (or stick with the default group "Users").
3. Add a Group ACL thats restricts that group to a certain language
4. Access the translation UI for that language as a user of that group

The "Suggest" feature is available as the group has the required permissions assigned and "Suggestions" are enabled for that component.

summary: issue with plural string (Android) for languages with different plural forms
description:
I noticed something strange related to plural string, but I'm not sure if it is a Weblate issue, or a TTK issue.

Some Asian languages (I noticed it for Chinese and Korean) don't have the grammatical concept of plural as fe. English (one, other), so Android only expects "other", for these languages.

Weblate displays one field in the interface, but puts its content in the "one" item, while "other" is also present in the [xml file](https://github.com/ruleant/getback_gps/commit/224650870c2ca47959d9aa6ff390f63244ee8b4c), but left empty. 
Android expects a value in "other", the value in "one" is ignored, resulting in an empty string when displaying it.

I suggest adding this cronjob to your openshift configuration for weblate.

French: `Voulez-vous vraiment supprimer « %s » ?`

Sometimes they use the unicode character `U+00A0`.

Is it possible to amend the check to allow ` ` or `U+00A0` as an alternative to a space?

es/ItemNames.po

summary: settings_example test for /dev/log is insufficient
description:
settings_example check if `/dev/log` is present to select the default log handler. If `/dev/log` is not present Weblate will still fail to start: since the syslog handler is still present in the config dict the logging module will try to initialise it. That will fail due to /dev/log missing and trigger an exception. As a workaround I added the following code just after the LOGGING definition:

``` python
if not os.path.exists('/dev/log'):
    del LOGGING['handlers']['syslog']
```

summary: escaping does not work on multiline strings (android) [$15 awarded]
description:
Special characters (', ", <, >) and newlines (\n) are not escaped in a multi-line string.
In [this commit](https://github.com/ruleant/getback_gps/commit/40ca02d31f1d2fe90ce7c24e6c38491ecc8699db#diff-1673efb4e556521d93d62e6dd0a6fbe9) string `license` is added by Weblate, but the `'` characters are not escaped, like in fe. the `copyright` string.

In [this commit](https://github.com/ruleant/getback_gps/commit/42a539c8f730328528164fd2a35ce36d195b09ca) the faulty special characters are escaped manually, the newline characters `\n` are added manually as well.

summary: Qt TS Format - Handle empty finished translations
description:
For Qt TS, initially:

``` xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE TS>
<TS version="2.0" language="en_US">
<context>
    <name>MainWindow</name>
    <message>
        <source>Hello world</source>
        <translation type="unfinished"></translation>
    </message>
</context>
```

If the translation is the same as the source however (e.g. translating from English to English), we generally just leave the translation as blank and mark it as finished so it becomes:

``` xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE TS>
<TS version="2.0" language="en_US">
<context>
    <name>MainWindow</name>
    <message>
        <source>Hello world</source>
        <translation></translation>
    </message>
</context>
```

So if the translation is empty and is marked as finished (doesn't have type="unfinished"), then we should use the source text as the translation instead marking it as untranslated and requiring translation.

In Qt applications, an empty finished translation just uses the source text.

summary: trans migration 0020_... has an improper default value when run against MySQL
description:
I have a brand new weblate installation that I am running on Ubuntu with MySQL as the backend. During the migrate command, particularly on trans/0020_auto__chg_field_change_translation__chg_field_change_unit.py I receive an error.

I can reproduce this error every time by recreating the weblate database and running ./manage.py migrate trans

The problem is on line 31:

```
db.alter_column('trans_change', 'translation_id', self.gf('django.db.models.fields.related.ForeignKey')(default=0, to=orm['trans.Translation']))
```

In particular, the default value is 0, and shouldn't be. Default values for foreign keys should generally be NULL, not 0 anyway, but in particular Django doesn't support 0 as an AutoField value for an ID if you're using MySQL, as of 2012-04-24.

This could be fixed by using default=None instead, but I didn't investigate anywhere that you might be detecting if Change.unit == 0 elsewhere in Weblate.

summary: Android translation with regional variations produces additional language dialects
description:
Android applications require resources to be placed into directories named "values-xx" where xx is language code.
That works unless you have regional variation/dialect. 
For dialect Android requires the directory to be contain letter "r" before dialect code:

http://androidcookbook.com/Recipe.seam?recipeId=358

> Android's practice here diverges slightly from Java's, in that Android uses a letter 'r' to denote regional variations, e.g., values-fr-rCA for French Canadian.

This cannot be worked around. The Android application will not even compile if you have dialect code without "r" prefix. (And this is not even mentioned in official Android documentation.)

So language code like pt_BR must be pt_rBR in Android file structure.
When importing such project to weblate we get following languages in weblate:
- Portuguese (pt-rBR)
- Portuguese
- Portuguese (pt-rPT)
- Portuguese (Brazil)
- Portuguese (Portugal)

Is there a way to give weblate a switch, when it's an Android project to will omit "r" when parsing the language dialect code?

summary: API | Support "query filters" for translation files
description:
### Describe the problem

Context : 

We have multiple translation projects that are shared between multiple development projects in a single source format. This is to avoid to translate the same keys in every projects.

Then, we use a script that import the translation files from different projects in the project required file format.

Weblate : 
- project: my-app, component: main, source lang: EN

Development projects : 
- app-ios : import my-app/main in format: iOS strings
- app-android: import my-app/main in format: Android String Resource

File : EN
```json
{
 "key1": "Hello",
 "key2": "World",
 "key3" : "weblate"
}
```

File : FR (not 100% translated)
```json
{
 "key1": "Hello"
}
```

The script will execute this : 
- app-ios : GET `/api/translations/my-app/main/fr/file/?format=strings`
- app-android : GET `/api/translations/my-app/main/fr/file/?format=aresource`


If we import the FR translations with the GET request, the result looks like this : 
Localizable.strings (iOS format)
```
 "key1": "Hello"
 "key2": "key2"
 "key3" : "key3"
```
Problem : If the key is not translated, it returns a row with the key as value.
That means in iOS it will display in the app the key as value in for this key.

strings.xml (Android format)
```
    <string name="key1">Hello</string>
    <string name="key2"></string>
    <string name="key3"></string>
```
Problem : If the key is not translated, it returns a row an empty value.
That means, in Android it will display in the app an empty text for this key.

The FR translation source file doesn't contains the keys: key2, key3. 

So, the formatted file receive from the request should not add the unexisting/untranslated keys.


### Describe the solution you'd like

If we use the weblate web interface we can do a customizable download and choose the file format and define a filter for the translations.  
We can download the needed file in format iOS and Android with the filter : `state:>=translated`.
It will return me exactly what I want : Only the translated keys in the format requested.

![Screenshot 2021-11-12 at 10 32 24](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/32476796/141452501-c0687a81-800c-49bb-98af-54afb50669c3.png)

We analysed the request done by the web interface :   
`https://translate.borrma.info/download/{project}/{component}/{lang}/csrfmiddlewaretoken=X&q=state:>=translated&format=strings`

Unfortunately, I cannot use it in my script because of authentication issue ?
We always receive a `404 - Access denied`. By the way, related to HTTP it should be a `403 - Forbidden` I guess.

The API `/api/translations/{project}/{component}/{lang}/file/` endpoint offers the query parameter `format`, but not the `q` parameter like the `download` request.

It would be great if you could implement this query parameter in the `/api/translations/{project}/{component}/{lang}/file/` endpoint too. 
This way we could specify the filters using the API, like we can use this feature on the web interface.

### Describe alternatives you've considered


### Screenshots

_No response_

### Additional context

Weblate API : 4.7.2. 

But in the latest version this feature is not present either.

**Is your feature request related to a problem? If so, please describe.**

Inline syntax within a message will sometimes be broken after machine translation with deepl as e.g. when translating to german ` will be replaced by " in most of the cases. 

Example:
The documentation software Sphinx uses the inline syntax for Links

```
This is a sentence with a `link <https://www.sphinx-doc.org/en/master/usage/restructuredtext/basics.html?highlight=link#external-links>`_ in Sphinx restructured text syntax.
```
This would be one message in weblate.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Deepl offers XML handling flags to not translate text in predefined tags.

```
"tag_handling=xml"
"ignore_tags=x"

```
When using the deepl API with weblate it would be helpful to have the opportunity to define some special chars and strings that will be escaped with xml-Tags that will be removed from the result afterwards.

e.g.

```
This is a sentence with a <x>`</x>link <x><</x>https://www.sphinx-doc.org/en/master/usage/restructuredtext/basics.html?highlight=link#external-links<x>>`_</x> in Sphinx restructured text syntax.
```




**Describe alternatives you've considered**

One approach could be to split the messages up further before sending them to deepl API, but deepl cannot maintain the grammar when sentences are chopped up too far.

summary: New users shouldn't be added as admin
description:
We are using hosted Weblate with a public (open source) project and have the review process enabled.
This means the user administration actually only has two different permission types available: `Admin` and `Review`
Adding a new user through the add user form adds the user with `Admin` permission.
Imho a new user should always gain the lowest permission available, in this case that would be `Review`.

Note: In another private project we have custom permissions and so the `Translate` permission is available. Adding a new user only grants `Translate` permissions, which seems fine.

**To Reproduce the issue**

Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Go to a public project (with enabled review process) on hosted.weblate.org where you have admin access
2. Go to the user management
3. Use the form to add a new user
4. See that the new user was added with admin permission

**Expected behavior**

The user should only have reviewer permission to avoid any security risks.

Hosted weblate

summary: Highlight unusual "space" characters in the editor
description:
Following up to #6360 it would be nice, if the translation editor could highlight unusual space characters, like it does for linebreaks. Right now it is not possible to tell a NBSP from a normal space and a zero width space disappears entirely.

summary: Issue reported when creating component via "Translate Document"
description:
When adding a new component to a project via **Translate Document**, a config error is shown which is not relevant.

1. In a project create a new component via **Translate Document**
2. Select the file you want to translate (e.g. demo-translation-file.odt)
3. Select the proposed Open Doc Format and confirm the default settings proposed by Weblate (the only change to the default I make/made is to disable **Edit base file**)
4. After the component is created, the following message is displayed.
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26718215/119977387-a6e75c00-bfb8-11eb-87a5-f6aa1f15cdad.png)

Contrary to the message, the component is fully functional and target languages can be added.
The error does  not seem to be an error and should be handled differently, ie. not shown in the UI.

**Describe the issue**

We're running a weblate instance on https://l10n.xwiki.org on which we have a project with 87 linked components. Recently a new language has been added to the root component which is also the biggest in term of number of keys (3609 keys). Since then is seems that we cannot commit the pending changes on this project: at first we had "only" 2Gb of RAM on the server, and we kept getting the process killed by OOM, so we started to increase the memory, we now have 5Gb of RAM and 5Gb of swap on the server. 
Now the process is not killed anymore apparently, but whenever I try to commit the pending changes nothing happens and/or I obtain the following error:
```
Timeout at /js/git/xwiki-platform/
The file lock '/var/weblate/data/vcs/xwiki-platform/xwiki-core-resources.lock' could not be acquired.
```

**I already tried**

As explained I already tried to put more memory on the server, without much success. I also try to disable celery to only trigger the commit changes synchronously, but without much success. 
I did not find any errors in the logs, except the one concerning the lock. 
Note that I checked the repository manually I rebased it already without any issue, and nothing is committed besides what's in https://github.com/xwiki/xwiki-platform/pull/1621 which I cannot really merge right now. Anyway I don't think that's an issue here. 
Also I noticed that the repository contained uncommitted files such as: `ApplicationResources_id.propertiesfor1d8o6`, where my filemask is `ApplicationResources_*.properties` and the new language is indeed indonesian. I tried several times to delete those files (which are empty), but apparently it doesn't change anything. 

So far the only move I can think of, would be to add more memory, but I don't know how much memory I'd need and usually we manage to run our Weblate server with only 2Gb so that's a bit worrying to need that much memory for adding a new language.

summary: Weblate detects illegal escape sequence in .po files too late
description:
As you might already know, I like to initialize translation components by uploading a full set (.pot and .po) files to weblate via zip. ;)

I did this and the component creation succeeded without error message. (Or at least I didn't notice)
But, as I found out later, the French .po file contained messages with "\r\n" in the translations.

I would have expected that this:

```
msgid ""
"Warning!\n"
"\n"
"The application of this product can be dangerous.\n"
"Please use it with care.\n"
"\n"
msgstr ""
"Avertissement !\r\n"
"\r\n"
"L'application de ce produit peut être dangereuse.\r\n"
"Veuillez l'utiliser avec précaution.\r\n"
"\r\n"
```

would already be detected when the .po file is analyzed for the first time.

What happened now was that (days) later, the .pot file was uploaded to weblate via the API and failed with a '400 Bad Request'.
Here's a snippet of the application's log of the API request/response:
```
Request     : multipart/form-data POST 'https://weblate.*****/api/translations/*****/*****/en/file/'

a/vcs/*****/*****/exe\\locale\\fr\\LC_MESSAGES\\*****.po:263: warning: internationalized messages should not contain the '\\r' escape sequence

... ad infinitum ;)
```

I would have expected that uploading the .pot file itself passes successfully, because it is not an error in the .pot file, but in one of the .po files that was uploaded earlier.

- Why is the project URL itself checked for validity?
- Why is the project URL mandatory at all?

Especially for an internal setup, it should be possible to make the URL:

- not mandatory or 
- turn the validation of the URL off or
- turn the certificate validation off

summary: Github Web UI shows weblate PRs strangely (unexpected commits are listed)
description:
**Describe the bug**

In our project, we prefer to have weblate use the "merge" style to incorporate changes from our main development branch.  Unfortunately, github ends up showing commits _already present_ in the main branch within the pull request!  Here's one such pull request in our project's history: https://github.com/adafruit/circuitpython/pull/3792

**To Reproduce the bug**

Here's the configuration and sequence of events that seem to happen:

1. In Hosted Weblate, configure a github project to "Merge style: Merge"
2. Create some translations and create a commit, which will create a github PR
3. Make some changes on the main branch by merging other PRs
4. Look at the PR created in step 2

**Expected behavior**

Only commits created by weblate are shown, not commits and changes from the main branch.

** Actual behavior **

Commits (and their changes) created by merging other PRs are visible in Weblate's PR

**Screenshots**

See https://github.com/adafruit/circuitpython/pull/3792

**Server configuration and status**

Weblate installation: Hosted weblate

**Additional context**

I first assumed this was a Github problem, but I manually created a PR https://github.com/adafruit/circuitpython/pull/3827 that goes through the same steps and github displays the PR as I expect, without listing commits from the main branch and the changes in those commits.  So the next hypothesis is that something is different about a weblate git merge than the one I did locally.  However, I can't see anything _specifically_ different in `git show --format=fuller`.  Pulling down the PR branch locally and looking at `git diff` and `git stat`, everything looks right.  So I'm puzzled, and still not 100% sure it's Weblate that is "in the wrong" here.  But this is negatively affecting our ability to review & approve translation PRs so I wanted to raise the issue here.

summary: Make Inclusion of weblate logs in Sentry configurable
description:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
We would like to use Sentry to monitor events generated by weblate. It appears that the sentry sdk is currently configured to ignore the `weblate` and `weblate.celery` loggers. As a result, the Sentry data paints and incomplete picture.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
A config variable is introduced which allows users to choose whether or not data from the `weblate` and `weblate.celery` loggers is sent to Sentry.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
We have considered forwarding log data to Sentry using a separate process, but we have been unable to find the logs in their default locations (However, it is possible that they were configured to appear elsewhere, the developer who configured the pod is out sick today).

**Additional context**
Above the code in question (`weblate/utils/errors.py:93-5`), there is a comment: 

> # Ignore Weblate logging, those should be reported as proper errors

It is not immediately clear why data sent to Sentry could not also be reported as an error. In fact, [your own documentation](https://docs.weblate.org/en/latest/admin/install.html?highlight=sentry#sentry) suggests using Sentry to monitor weblate and celery errors, and yet both of these loggers are explicitly being ignored. What exactly does "built-in support" mean in this context?

summary: Add syntax highlight and quick actions for reStructuredText markup constructs
description:
At least it should highlight roles and the ability to insert these parts unchanged by `Alt+<number>` (like is it done for XML or HTML tags or format placeholders).

In the simplest case reStructuredText role looks like this:
```rst
:role_name:`role text`
or
`role text`:role_name:
```
Also special cases:
```rst
*emphasis*, **strong emphasis**, `interpreted text` or ``inline literal``
`hyperlink reference`_ or `anonymus hyperlink reference`__, also with `alias <aliased>`_
[#footnote]_, also [#]_, or [*]_, or [2]_, or [CITATION]_
```
Also it is good to support roles from Sphinx, many of which look like this:
```rst
:ref:`Optional title <some_identifier>`
:py:class:`ClassName`
:py:meth:`~Queue.Queue.get`
```
Ideally, this markup should also not change with machine translation, but I don't know if this is possible in principle.

**Additional info:**

- [reStructuredText Markup Specification](https://docutils.sourceforge.io/docs/ref/rst/restructuredtext.html).
- [reStructuredText Interpreted Text Roles](https://docutils.sourceforge.io/docs/ref/rst/roles.html).
- [Standard Sphinx roles](https://www.sphinx-doc.org/en/master/usage/restructuredtext/roles.html).

summary: Extend "Customize JSON output" addon with option to remove keys with empty value
description:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
When having a HTML5 application and e.g. using ngx-translate as translation provider, this allows to specifcy a fallback mechanism, where in case a key is not found it falls back to the default language. Hence, if a certain value from source is not translated to a target language, this specific key should not appear in the target language's json.
This is generally the case when `Template for new translations:` is left open / unspecified as:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8058166/85262226-c94e2c80-b46d-11ea-8f42-05d574f4aa5a.png)

Still, an empty value can be created (despite of above's configuration) if a context once has been translated, later on the value has been deleted and saved again ( weblate). As example, the history of following value shows this case:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8058166/85262748-817bd500-b46e-11ea-8ca7-989c782d0a1d.png)

With this, the `de.json` (as per example above) ends up with an entry as following

```json
{
    "LOGIN": {
        "ACTION": ""
    }
}
```

If this `de.json` is provided as German translation the for `LOGIN.ACTION` it will display an empty string `""` and fallback to English won't work.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Extend the `Customize JSON output` addon with the following option:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8058166/85265040-f3a1e900-b471-11ea-97c6-dbdf2099f668.png)


The idea is that the addon can be configured (`true / false`) to remove keys with empty values. Furthermore, if this results in empty objects and/or lists, also those shall be removed. 

With the given example above, the extended addon may needs to run several times / recursively, where the first criteria would generate:

```json
{
    "LOGIN": {
    }
}
```

and a second run would generate:

```json
{
}
```

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
This could be done with a post processing on the repository which receives translations from weblate by using e.g. [jq](https://github.com/stedolan/jq), with a call similar to 

```
jq walk(if type == "object" then with_entries(select(.value != null and .value != "" and .value != [] and .value != {})) else . end)
```

Drawback is, that the receiving repository needs an additional "compile" step to prepare the translation resources, and hence the json's cannot be used as delivered by Weblate, out of the box.

Hence it would be preferred, if this kind of cleaned-up output could be achieved by Weblate directly.

summary: Evaluate usage of django-compressor
description:

* Drop django-compressor usage

summary: Consecutive duplicated words is triggered when translating repetitions
description:
**Describe the bug**
The “Consecutive duplicated words” check is triggered even if the repeat is a translation of repeated words in the source string. This is false positive and I expect not triggered check in that case.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Go to https://hosted.weblate.org/translate/andors-trail/game-content/ru/?checksum=e794e9c184b2be2f

**Expected behavior**
No warning.

I think it should also count the number of repetitions in the source string and trigger warning only if the number of repetitions in the translation is different. For example:
```po
# :Source string:     two word groups with two and three repetitions
# :Translated string: two word groups with two and three repetitions
# :Result:            no warning
msgid "HAH HAH! HEH HEH HEH!"
msgstr "ХАХ ХАХ! ХЕ ХЕ ХЕ!"

# :Source string:     two word groups with two and three repetitions
# :Translated string: two word groups with two and two (less than source) repetitions
# :Result:            warning
msgid "HAH HAH! HEH HEH HEH!"
msgstr "ХАХ ХАХ! ХЕ ХЕ!"

# :Source string:     two word groups with two and three repetitions
# :Translated string: two word groups with three (more than source) and two repetitions
# :Result:            warning
msgid "HAH HAH! HEH HEH HEH!"
msgstr "ХАХ ХАХ ХАХ! ХЕ ХЕ ХЕ!"

# :Source string:     two word groups with two and three repetitions
# :Translated string: one (less than source) word group with two repetitions
# :Result:            warning
msgid "HAH HAH! HEH HEH HEH!"
msgstr "ХАХ ХАХ!"

# :Source string:     two word groups with two and three repetitions
# :Translated string: three (more than source) word groups with two, 
#                     three and two repetitions
# :Result:            warning
msgid "HAH HAH! HEH HEH HEH!"
msgstr "ХАХ ХАХ! ХЕ ХЕ ХЕ! ХИ ХИ!"
```

**Additional context**
As mentioned in footer, hosted.weblate.org works on Weblate 4.1-dev.

summary: Expand search and replace capabilities
description:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Currently search and replace tool too dumb:
1. It finds all substrings matching the entered search string. This leads to problems when you need to replace a word that is often found as a substring in other words. For example, if in Russian I want to replace the word “еще” with “ещ***ё***” (“more”), there will be a lot of garbage replaces with replacements like “п***еще***ра” -> “п***ещё***ра” (“cave”), “в***еще***ство” -> “в***ещё***ство” (“substance”) or “в***еще***й” -> “в***ещё***й” (“things”). The flag “search only whole words” is needed.
2. Since the number of replacements is limited to 250, sooner or later such garbage replaces will completely clog this limit and the tool will become useless.
3. There is no way to choose specific replacements. For example, we have the phrase “Но все ***все*** всегда знали.” (“But everyone always knew ***all***.”) and I want to replace second “все” to “всё” (“all”), but in the phrase there is another (first) word “все” (“everyone”) that does not need to be replaced. It should turn out “Но все ***всё*** всегда знали.” Now it is impossible (even if will be implemented paragraph 1).

**Describe the solution you'd like**
1. Add flag “only whole words”.
2. Add ability to choose replacements in one string, not only “all or nothing”.
3. Maybe add some color indication which replacements are selected, because now it is difficult to distinguish which replacements will be made when click to “Replace” button. A checkbox mark is too subtle.

summary: Add description field to glossary term
description:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Sometimes term has more than once appropriate translations, which can be used in different contexts — for example, species name or proper name. In first case name should be translated, but on second case it might be transliterated.

In such cases, it would be nice to have two identical terms with different translations and indicate in a note when which one to use. This note is then displayed in the glossary widget along with the term.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Add description field to glossary term, in which the translator can, for example provide additional information on the use of the term in an ambiguous environment, or clarify what the term means, or why such a translation was chosen.

**Expected behavior**
Filter `has:comment` should shown all comments. Or, at least, one more filter is needed to show all translation strings with comments on the source strings.

summary: Use string source location from a master .pot file if missing in .po
description:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
I have a C gettext based project, where `po/*.po` contains the translations, and `po/$appname.pot` contains the master translation template. 

The .pot file contains source location information for all 'msgids'.

The individual `.po` files have source location removed, as this information is considered a redundant duplication of what is already present in the `.pot` file that adds to the size of the git repo for no gain, and harms the signal/noise ratio of any commits updating the `.po` files.

The intent is to never modify the `.po` files in upstream in order to eliminate conflicts with commits that weblate makes to the `.po` files. Thus upstream will just periodically update the `.pot`, and not run `msgmerge` for the `.po` files.

Instead the `msgmerge` add-on is enabled in weblate so that it will update the `*.po` files when new strings appear in the `.pot`.  The `Remove locations of translated strings` option is to used to prevent weblate re-adding source locations when it does this update.

The end result though is that when looking at the strings needing translation for a language in the weblate UI, no information about the source location is presented AFAICT. This is not good for translators, as they lack context if they need to understand more about the strings being translated.

I presume this same problem would be present even if not using the `msgmerge` add-on  in weblate at all, and letting the project run it upstream to update msgids in the `.po` files. So the `msgmerge` add-on and its `no location` option are probably tangential this problem.


**Describe the solution you'd like**
When the `.po` file has no source locations, the source locations in the `.pot` file mentioned for the  `Template for new translations` setting could be used in their place.


**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Even though the `.pot` file stored in git has locations present, this information is still liable to be out of date. Source locations can change after any single commit, so the only way to ensure freshness would be for the upstream project to re-generate the `.pot` on every commit. This is not very desirable as those updates have poor signal/noise ratio with locations changing very frequently.

The ideal situation is for weblate to have 100% up to date source string locations at all times. 

It isn't practical for weblate to run the application's actual build step to re-generate the `.pot` file itself, as there are so many different build systems involved and some of them can be insanely slow or have non-trivial dependencies.  Many projects, especially those on GitForges, have some kind of automated CI system. It is potentially quite easy for such a CI system to publish a new `.pot` file on a URL. Weblate could periodically fetch this URL, and this new .pot could then be used as the data for string source locations.

summary: Support GitHub pull requests without the need of a fork
description:
It seems like the default way the GitHub integration system works is by creating a fork of the source repository, then pushing branches to it, then making pull requests from those branches to the master remote. This introduces some difficulties when working with a continuous integration setup, since then the CI runs will need to be configured to both allow building forked branches and potentially even need to allow sharing credentials/secrets with the forked branch. See CircleCI for example: ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/16181067/82046316-ee9e8c80-96b0-11ea-931e-22476b02cd62.png)
Transcription of the CircleCI options
Build forked pull requests Run builds for pull requests from forks. CircleCI will automatically update the commit status shown on GitHub's pull request page. --- Pass secrets to builds from forked pull requests Run builds for fork pull request changes with this project's configuration, environment variables, and secrets. There are serious security concerns with this setting (see the documentation for details.) If you have SSH keys, sensitive env vars or AWS credentials stored in your project settings and untrusted forks can make pull requests against your repo, then this option isn't for you!
**Solution** Would it be possible to change the way the GitHub integration system works? Since Weblate can ask for write permissions, another option would be to: 1. Create a local branch for translations that's automatically rebased onto the source branch. 2. On a Weblate push, make a pull request from this branch to the source branch. Both should be on the master remote. Then there would be no need for a fork. **Alternative** The alternative right now is to allow forks of private repos, and to then configure CI to allow building forks, and potentially (depending on each setup) to pass credentials to the forks. **Additional context** Weblate version 3.11.3 --- Want to back this issue? **[Post a bounty on it!](https://www.bountysource.com/issues/91562877-support-github-pull-requests-without-the-need-of-a-fork?utm_campaign=plugin&utm_content=tracker%2F253393&utm_medium=issues&utm_source=github)** We accept bounties via [Bountysource](https://www.bountysource.com/?utm_campaign=plugin&utm_content=tracker%2F253393&utm_medium=issues&utm_source=github).

summary: Only show "Shapings" if count > 1
description:
This is a small follow up to https://github.com/WeblateOrg/weblate/issues/3141

**Pre-requiste**

- *Shapings* is configured with regex `#(S|M|L)$`
- Key / msgid exists with `mykey#M`
- Base-key is nowhere else in use, means
  - `mykey` ... does not exist
  - `mykey#S` ... does not exist
  - `mykey#L` ... does not exist

**Effect**
Weblate successfully detects `mykey#M` as a Shaping and shows it:
- Under *Things to check*
- Under *Shapings* tab
- Count is `1` (itself)

**Improvement**
If `count==1` it does not make sense to show *Things to check* and *Shapings* tab. Please introduce a condition to show *Shapings* only if `count>1`

All commits squashed into one commit regardless of addon.

summary: Repetition check
description:
Some platforms/tools have checks for repetition, which is the error that happens most often.

When something is very complex, it is easy to stop, think, and then carry on from the word already put down onwards. It can also happen when rewriting a sentence, ending up with two parts that share a repeated word in its midst.

For example this this is an example of a repeated word.

Example and example, fine. "This this" etc. is almost always an error.
If not an outright error, it is often best avoided, so quality would improve a lot overall with a check that (in most languages) has very few false positives.

summary: Explicitely warn using non-practical language codes
description:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

We have discussed this shortly at FOSDEM 2020. The same [Dutch language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch_language) is used in the Netherlands, Belgium and Suriname. Of course, there are local variations, dialects and customs, but in general for software, only one Dutch translation is made. The [official rules](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch_Language_Union) on spelling, grammar, etc. are identical.

However, the following language codes and locales exist:
1. `nl` Dutch in general
2. `nl_AN` Dutch in Netherlands Antilles (**was** a constituent country with the Kingdom of the Netherlands)
3. `nl_AW` Dutch in Aruba (**is** a constituent country with the Kingdom of the Netherlands)
4. `nl_BE` Dutch in the Kingdom of Belgium
5. `nl_NL` Dutch in the Kingdom of the Netherlands
6. `nl_SR` Dutch in the Republic of Suriname

Many many times, developers and translators are not aware that only one Dutch translation needs to be made and/or think that they should choose the language code as specific as possible. Usually this is done with the best of intentions.

In the past en present, this resulted in often two or three translations all trying to do the same translation. Consolidating is sometimes difficult as personal style or choice of words can differ of the different translations, and not that the official language differs. In short, it creates unintentionally a lot of extra work in translating and managing a translation and subsequent software release where the translation is used.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Proper internationalized and localized software will switch to e.g. a language code `nl` if a more specific version such as `nl_NL` or `nl_BE` is not available but requested by the operating system.

New and existing projects on Weblate should warn translation maintainers when a language code of `nl_*` is used and motivate them to refactor and consolidate translations to `nl` only.

A similar case could be made for `en_NZ` and `en_IE` representing English in New Zealand and Ireland with respect to `en_GB` English in Great Britain. But of the 20 country codes related to English, this is more tricky to define with American, etc.

Of course, the translation maintainer should be able to ignore this warning, but should also be able to reread it at a later point in time somewhere in the settings of a project.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

Simply not allowing translations to `nl_*`, only `nl`, but that is too forceful and unwanted because some exceptions on for example texts on national law can be found, but these are an extremely tiny amount of the translations. Usually exceptions are found in software content and not in the translation of the software buttons, labels, etc.

**Additional context**

Implementation could be via these configurations:
* `nl:nl_*` (when regex is supported) otherwise `nl:nl_NL nl_BE nl_SR nl_AW nl_AN`
* `en_GB:en_NZ en_IE`

Also language code formats such as `ca_ES@valencia` and `ca_ES-valencia` should be supported.

summary: Translating and priorizing Glossary
description:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

In our service there are some key terms for which we need translation consistency. We use the glossary for that. Think of the term "synchronise" for a service like dropbox, or the term "invite" for a service like facebook. You need consistent translations for that and the start and the glossary seems like a good tool.

Our current process is to invite "experts users" to weblate first, then follow up so that they translate the glossary first, so that it will help the rest of the contributors. (we export/import glossaries to help).

It frustrates us that there is no way to translate the glossary from the source language. You need to re-write the glossary from scratch and cannot use aid from machine translation.

It is also frustrating that some contributors will join and start translating before key terms in the glossary have been translated.

We also think that the Glossary is hidden on the right hand, contributors don't realize their existence if we don't alert them, or until they have gained a lot of experience.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

There should be an option to mark in project or components called "translate glossary first", and the glossary terms to be offered in the normal translation workflow as terms to start translation with. 

If the option is not selected empty glossaries should offer: do you want to translate from source language? 

It could also be possible to limit the glossary translation to distinguished terms that could be ticked in the source language's glossary as "key terms". 

To boost glossary usability, an alert should be made around the input field when a source string includes terms in the glossary. this could be implemented as an icon (!) include glossary terms. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

As an alternative we onboard contributors in parallel. Or course It could be possible to onboard users in an automated way.

summary: Implement native GitHub/GitLab pull requests
description:

description:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Not sure if it's a bug or works as intended, but comments in Android string files and Java properties files work differently.
In Java properties if you leave a blank line between the comment line and string line the comment is not shown in Weblate. As an example, here is a Java properties file:
```
string1=String 1
# This comment will NOT be shown

string2=String 2

#This comment will be shown
string3= String 3
```

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/36223356/70701508-843a8800-1cdd-11ea-90c1-661ee04c5545.png)

```
    <!-- This comment should NOT be shown -->

    <string name="string2">String 2</string>
    <!-- This comment should be shown -->

```
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/36223356/70701966-51dd5a80-1cde-11ea-8f6a-2795cadd6ce5.png)
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/36223356/70701985-5a359580-1cde-11ea-9c62-bab7691fd04a.png)

summary: Provide a secondary source language in case "Monolingual base language file" is marked as editable
description:
## Situation

For translation we run a three step approach:

1. **Developer** to create and provide SWEnglish / Developer-English. We call it `template`
1. **Harmonize** `template` into a proper and polished `en`
1. **Translator** to go for further translations based on `en` released from Harmonize step

In our weblate configuration we created an artificial language called `template`, what represents this English from developer perspective

This means for Harmonize:
- Source: `template`
- Target: `en`

This means for Translator:
- Source: `en`
- Target: any other language

## Expected behavior

- In in Harmonize step, when user is editing `en`, present `en` as "Translation **English**" and `template` as "Source"
  - Also in this case the secondary base language `template` provides the comprehensive list of contexts (keys/msgid's)
- When string has changed in `template`, show in the `Component`/`en` overview tab that `Strings marked for edit` due to secondary source has changed

Remark:
- In Translator step, `en` shall be the source language, as it already is today
- Also `en` then provides the list of context (keys/msgid's), as it already is today

## Expected configuration

In `Component` configuration dialogue (e.g. Django Admin Interface), when:
- [x] Edit base file (allowed) ... is ticked, provide an additional drop-down underneath to `Select secondary source language`
- In this case `template` should be picked then.

## Expected behavior of Addons

### Cleanup translation files

If secondary source language is set, enhance for a two step approach:

1. Cleanup `en` against `template`
1. Cleanup all other languages against `en`

(Any other Addon which would need enhancement due to two step approach?)

## Expected behavior of `Project`/`Component`/`Language` > Tools > Automatic translation

- If *Automatic translation* is started from `Project`/`Component`/`en` and secondary source language is set as `template`, then take `template` as source for match making.
- If *Automatic translation* is started from `Project`/`Component`/`Any other than en`, then take primary source language `en` as base for match making.

This shall apply to both, component based automatic translation and to machine based automatic translation with fuzzy match making.

summary: XWiki formats support
description:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
As part of XWiki development we manipulate three different kind of translation formats:
  - standard java properties
  - XWiki XML properties
  - XWiki full pages

If the first format is a standard one, the two others are really specific to XWiki, and we need to keep them for backward compatibility.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
It would be nice to have an API to define a transformation, from a monolingual source file, to its translation. To be able to define custom translation formats.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

Basically our workflow is the following:
  - our XML files are automatically transformed to properties on update events
  - the translations are performed on those properties file
  - on pre commit event the properties are transformed back to the right format
  - on post commit event, we clean the commit to remove the files we don't want on our VCS

This solution works, but it's costly for us since we have to maintain our scripts, and it prevents us to use some nice features of Weblate such as the discovery addon.

summary: Show different string lengths of same term/message together (responsive design)
description:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

For software running on different form factors, there is a common practice to define texts in several shapings differing in lengths (e.g. Monday->Mon->M). The software following responsive design principles then picks up the according text length according to the current form factor.

Typically the software follows a key convention for such texts such that the keys have a common part and a varying part such and short/medium/long as a suffix.

However, the translators do not see these texts together, each entry is shown as an independent entity. So translation errors can happen such as:
* not following length rules (e.g. short translation longer than the medium translation)
* not following the same semantic for different lengths of a message.

So, the translators need a way of seeing different shapings of a term/message together.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

* The keys follow a certain pattern such as `<key><separator><shaping>`, e.g. `monday#s`
* The separator or a regular expression for defining shapings in keys can be configured in component settings in Weblate
* Weblate then will group/show these entries always together
* Weblate doesn't need to interpret shapings further, as the software developer can define different max-lengths for each shaping entry

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

Alt. 1: If the message has multiple shapings, provide a `Shapings` tab similar to the `Nearby strings` tab underneath, and show other shapings of the message there, so the user knows immediately there are other shapings to consider. Mock screen:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/30393701/67404382-989eb600-f5b3-11e9-81ae-5e0b70c1c072.png)

Alt. 2: Show shapings in the upper part of the window, similar to plurals.

Alt. 3: Provide a `Nearby keys` tab similar to the `Nearby strings` tab, showing the nearby strings based on key proximity rather than physical proximity in the translation file.

Alt. 4: (No Weblate change needed): Order the translation files by keys so that nearby strings is the same as nearby keys.

Alt. 5: Extend the addon interface of Weblate to be able to customize translator frontend, so such functionality can be added on-demand.

**Additional context**

Example project: [locale file from npm moment](https://github.com/moment/moment/blob/develop/locale/en-gb.js), uses xxx, xxxShort, xxxMin.

summary: Provide data languages scheme based on programming languages
description:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
We are using Weblate for a Java project that is using the standard Java locales. However the language code defined in Weblate is not mapping the language codes defined in Java locales: for example, for the Chinese support, we have this for Java (extracted from https://www.oracle.com/technetwork/java/javase/java8locales-2095355.html):

```
Chinese (zh) | China (CN) |   | (Hans) | zh-CN |  
Chinese (zh) | Singapore (SG) |   | (Hans) | zh-SG(*) |  
Chinese (zh) | Hong Kong (HK) |   | (Hant) | zh-HK |  
Chinese (zh) | Taiwan (TW) |   | (Hant) | zh-TW
```

where Weblate have the following:
```
# Translators: Language name, ISO code: za
    ('za', _('Zhuang'), 2, 'n != 1'),
    # Translators: Language name, ISO code: zh_Hans
    ('zh_Hans', _('Chinese (Simplified)'), 1, '0'),
    # Translators: Language name, ISO code: zh_Hant
    ('zh_Hant', _('Chinese (Traditional)'), 1, '0'),
    # Translators: Language name, ISO code: zh_Hant_HK
    ('zh_Hant_HK', _('Chinese (Hong Kong)'), 1, '0'),
```

**Describe the solution you'd like**
It could be really useful to provide different schemes of languages, depending on the programming language and their own standard language code mapping.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
For now we'll amend manually our list of languages from the admin, but it's a bit tedious.
