summary: Automatic translation with source Machine translation "Weblate" runs in server time-out
description:
**Describe the bug**
Having a component and applying *Automatic translation* with source *Machine translation - Weblate* (weblate internal machine), fuzzy match (Score threshold) set to 75, runs into server time out *504 Gateway Time-out -- Ther server didn't respond in time.*
- Target component has about 550 strings for a specific language
- Weblate machine has a pool of about 30'000 strings for this language, provided from other components

**Cross check**
Reducing Target component to about 10 strings, rest remains same as above, works properly.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Go to component, select target language (e.g. `fr`)
2. Click on 'Tools -> Automatic translation'
3. Settings: 
  - `Search filter : Not translated strings`
  - `Automatic translation source : Machine translation`
  - `Machine translation engines : Weblate`
  - `Score threshold : 75`
4. Click on `Process`
5. See error

**Expected behavior**
No server time-out happens.

**Solution Idea**
On click `Process`, the UI switches to a `In Progress` dialogue in context of the current language, e.g. with progress bar and/or busy indicator, whilst machine translation happens asynchronously in the background. Maybe, during this happens, the current language is locked for editing.

Might be similar to #372 , but in context of `Automatic translation`

summary: Priority flag
description:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
We are using po files to translate a series of manpages. I'd like to help translator translate most viewed text by directing them to the translation of selected source files. Now, the translation is managed in the order of the po file which is alphabetical only.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
It would be great if we could provide a drop-down list of source files names, and when selecting one name, only have the strings from this file available for further processing (untranslated, fuzzy...).

I think it would also be useful for software translations too where the most viewed strings in the sofware could be translated in priority. This is a good way to provide positive feed-back to translators, when their work is quickly visible, even if not complete.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Another choice would be to split the files into multiple po files, but that would have a few drawbacks, firstly because the script would require to merge back things when generating the output, with chances of conflicts.

There might be some simpler solutions, but I'm not aware of them.

**Additional context**

This is a special context of documentation translation.

summary: Allow to increase the limit of 200 characters length for components filemask/template
description:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
We use Weblate in the project [XWiki](https://github.com/xwiki/xwiki-platform) with some custom scripts to be able to manage various kind of resource files that exists in Maven submodules.
The problem is that 200 characters is to limited for the hierarchy of submodules we now have, for example I recently tried to add the following filemask: 
`.translation/xwiki-platform-core/xwiki-platform-security/xwiki-platform-security-authentication/xwiki-platform-security-authentication-ui/src/main/resources/XWiki/Authentication/Translations_*.properties` which is 203 characters long.

This limitation also apply on the template path, see:
`.translation/xwiki-platform-core/xwiki-platform-security/xwiki-platform-security-authentication/xwiki-platform-security-authentication-ui/src/main/resources/XWiki/Authentication/Translations_en.properties`. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**
We already patched the database to increase the size of filemask/template columns, but the maxlength put in the Django model (https://github.com/WeblateOrg/weblate/blob/master/weblate/trans/models/component.py#L238) still prevents to call `import_json` with such paths.
It would be nice to have a way to configure this limitation. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
As said we already patched the DB. I also edited the linked component.py file in my own instance to put 400 instead of 200 as maxlength. So far I didn't notice any issue with doing that, but I guess I'll need to do it at each upgrade which is not nice.

summary: Introduce plurality handling based on angular and ngx-translate file format and schema
description: # Situation In web development angular together with ngx-translate is one of the most commonly used combination to handle texts and translations. Weblate supports this in its basic functionality by allowing import as JSON / JSON nested file structure. As stated in weblate documentation, this file format doesn't allow for plurality # Request Introduce another JSON based file format and according treatment in weblate to cover standard behavior of angular's plurality handling. Format might be called *JSON angular i18nPlural*. # Example Given a simple example of a kind of a count-down with years, months and days, the basic HTML structure may looks as following: ```html {{ roundedRemTime.years | i18nPlural: ('DATE_DIFF_MAP' | translate) ['YEAR'] }} {{ roundedRemTime.months | i18nPlural: ('DATE_DIFF_MAP' | translate) ['MONTH'] }} {{ roundedRemTime.days | i18nPlural: ('DATE_DIFF_MAP' | translate) ['DAY'] }} ``` Therefore, an `en.json` exists, which provides the following key-value structure: ```json "DATE_DIFF_MAP": { "YEAR": { "=0": "", "=1": "# year", "other": "# years" }, "MONTH": { "=0": "", "=1": "# month", "other": "# months" }, "DAY": { "=0": "", "=1": "# day", "other": "# days" } } ``` According [angular i18nPluralPipe](https://angular.io/api/common/I18nPluralPipe) the very last key element is essential to map a given value to a string in order to pluralize. Where all key elements starting with `=` are treated as cases with exact match and `other` catches everything else. Additionally, `#` is the placeholder to be replaced with the input value and to be rendered together with the rest of the string, e.g. resulting in `1 year`, `2 years`, `3 years`, etc. Based on this rule, weblate should detect a situation as given above and e.g. represent the value behind `DATE_DIFF_MAP.YEAR` as one context with plurality. This would allow to properly catch-up with translating languages with more complex pluralization rules, e.g. resulting in `cz.json` as ```json "DATE_DIFF_MAP": { "YEAR": { "=0": "", "=1": "# rok", "=2": "# roky", "=3": "# roky", "=4": "# roky", "other": "# let" }, ... } ``` # Expected/proposed behavior - Treat the cases for `>=1` and `other` according the language's specific pluralization rules where - `=1` is singular - `>1` and `other` match the required plurals - Special treatment for `=0` - if `"=0": ""` (empty string) then don't show for translation at all - if `"=0": "year elapsed"` (not empty string) only then offer for translation to other languages # Alternatives - Use alternative format as gettext (po) for translation which already covers plurality properly - Pro: Loaders are available as [ngx-translate-gettext-loader](https://github.com/UnifiedFactory/ngx-translate-gettext-loader) - Cons: Requires parsing first in browser, performance issue, whereas json is directly applicable - Cons: No preferred option and also not common in angular/ngx-translate community. - Use e.g. xliff as [angular i18n](https://angular.io/guide/i18n) - Pro: xliff supports plurality - Cons: Requires compilation, direct deployment not possible, whereas json is directly applicable - Cons: No preferred option and also not common in angular/ngx-translate community. - Use i18next (already known by weblate) - Cons: would need to rework original projects code which is currently based on angular/ngx-translate

summary: Performance boost: Component Discovery Addon should not be available to repo links
description:
**Describe the bug**
Any time a VCS pull is made on a component, it triggers the component discovery process on the component linked to an actual repository and on all its linked childs, which makes the pull operation terribly slow.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Configure a Git repository with a lot of files.
2. Go to Weblate and create a project with one component linked to one of the files in the Git repo (let's name this component "master-component").
3. Install the Component Discovery addon on master-component to match all the other files in the Git repo.
4. It will take a while for Weblate to create all the components, but that's OK. Wait for it to finish.
5. Modify one of the files in the Git repo (e.g., add a new term to translate)
6. Back to Weblate, go to the repository management view of one of the components and perform a Pull operation. This will be very slow.

**Expected behavior**
Once the pull button is pressed, the process to sync the repo should not be that time consuming.

The method Component::update_branch (in file trans/models/component.py) triggers a vcs_post_update on "master-component" and all of its linked childs. This eventually produces a call to post_update on each of the addons installed in the child component. And here lies the problem: since each linked child has the component discovery addon installed, it will be run. 

I understand the need to run the component discovery on the "master-component", but not on its children.

**Easy fix**
I have managed to temporarily fix it by modifying the method DiscoveryAddon::post_update (within file addons/discovery.py):

```
def post_update(self, component, previous_head):
        if not component.is_repo_link: 
                self.perform()
```

However, I am wondering whether a better solution would be to not install the Component Discovery addon automatically on child components (i.e., those created by Weblate as a result of the component discovery itself).

**Notes on performance**
With ~350 child components, the previous fix makes the Pull operation run 7.5 times faster.

summary: Support for Qt 5 Linguist TS files
description:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Qt 5 and Qt 4 TS files are similar to each other, however, they have some differences:
* `<message>` tag no more uses `utf8="true"` tag, the codepage is always UTF8 or specified in the header of entire TS file.
* Version of TS is 2.1 on Qt 5 while 2.0 on Qt 4
* Vanished messages are now marking with `type="vanished"` in Qt 5 and `type="obsolete"` in Qt 4. However, Qt 4's "obsolete" is still work on Qt Linguist of Qt 5, but no more coming by default.

In most, Qt 5 translations are working well, except messages are marked as "vanished" are appearing as "alive" when they are must be same as "obsolete".

**Describe the solution you'd like**
For now because of "vanished" tag, obsolete messages are appearing as "alive" when they are must be not shown. The first solution is applying the [patch to the `translate` dependent library directly](https://github.com/translate/translate/pull/3902/commits/fb637f151c8c2ee2f5dc95cf41327901cdc34de6) which resolves this problem without modifying of WebLate itself.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
However, when using the older `translate` library, the problem will still appear. Therefore it's would be needed to copy the patched implementation of TS file parser into the WebLate directly to support Qt 5 translations independently from the version of `translate` library.

**Additional context**
An example of Qt 5 translation that has vanished messages are marked by the new way: https://github.com/Wohlstand/OPL3BankEditor/blob/master/src/translations/opl3bankeditor_fr_FR.ts

summary: Respect default (Visual Studio) resx formatting
description:
## Description

Weblate format _resx_ files differently than Visual Studio, namely:
* Line 1: single quotes are used instead of double quotation marks:
    * Default resx: `<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>`
    * Weblate: `<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?>`
* Line 1: encoding is capitalized instead of lower case:
    * Default resx: `<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>`
    * Weblate: `<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?>`
* Node `<xsd:schema ...>`: parameters order is changed:
    * Default resx: `<xsd:schema id="root" xmlns="" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema" xmlns:msdata="urn:schemas-microsoft-com:xml-msdata">`
    * Weblate: `<xsd:schema xmlns="" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema" xmlns:msdata="urn:schemas-microsoft-com:xml-msdata" id="root">`
* Self-closing nodes `< />`: the space character before the self-closing tag is removed:
    * Default resx: `<xsd:import namespace="http://www.w3.org/XML/1998/namespace" />`
    * Weblate: `<xsd:import namespace="http://www.w3.org/XML/1998/namespace"/>`
* Last line: a new line is added at the end of file:
    * Default resx: 
        ```
        </root>
        No newline at end of file
        ```
    * Weblate: 
        ```
        </root>
        
        ```

## Steps to reproduce

Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Format resx file through Visual Studio.
2. Translate some strings through Weblate. Commit, Push.
3. Notice the changes in the commit.

## Expected behavior

Weblate should respect the default resx formatting offered by Visual Studio.

## Screenshot

This shows a git diff (inverted compared to the steps above - red = Weblate version, green = VS version):

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3851902/59201460-c8b46200-8b9a-11e9-877f-9918d026ff8d.png)

summary: remove translations from components via API
description:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

A new admin enabled the "Language Consistency" plugin, which filled all the components with empty translations.  This makes it harder to manage, especially with the squash/rebase workflow.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

A way to use the existing _remove_ function via the API.  E.g. https://hosted.weblate.org/remove/f-droid/website-tutorials/eu/

The API could use the same confirmation string, e.g. the whole project/component/language triplet.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

It is possible via the web UI, but that is really time consuming to do for more than a few translations.

**Additional context**

Here's the script that I wrote to do this, it is only lacking the API call to do the actual remove:

```python
import os
import requests
import time

components_url = 'https://hosted.weblate.org/api/projects/f-droid/components/'
translations_url = 'https://hosted.weblate.org/api/components/f-droid/%s/translations/'

r = requests.get(components_url)
r.raise_for_status()
data = r.json()

components = []
for component in data['results']:
    components.append(component['slug'])

deleteme = dict()
for component in components:
    r = requests.get(translations_url % component)
    r.raise_for_status()
    data = r.json()
    for result in data['results']:
        if result['translated'] == 0 \
           and result['translated_words'] == 0 \
           and result['translated_percent'] == 0:
            language_code = result['language_code']
            if language_code not in deleteme:
                deleteme[language_code] = []
            deleteme[language_code].append(component)

for language, components in deleteme.items():
    for component in sorted(components):
        os.system('firefox https://hosted.weblate.org/projects/f-droid/%s/%s/#delete'
                  % (component, language))
```

summary: Check rendered string length
description:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Weblate already supports limiting text length by `maxlength:N` flag. However this is not good enough in some cases when the space is really limited and font rendering should be taken into consideration.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Add a check which would render the text using defined font and check actual size of the rendered text.

This comes with some tricky pieces though:

* Needs fonts, probably those could be managed in Weblate per project
  * There might be different fonts for different languages
* Needs more parameters for check
  * Font name (or rather family defined in Weblate, see above)
  * Font size
  * Font weight
  * Kerning (optional)
  * Allowed width
  * Allowed number of lines (optional)
* Pillow which we use for this in the widgets is probably not flexible enough, this will need Pango
* Pango (contrary to Pillow) can not load directly font, needs first to tweak FONTCONFIG_PATH/FONTCONFIG_FILE to change fontconfig setup to find the fonts

Implementation details:

* Font files management (4)
  * Per project
  * Upload TTF/OTF font, store file, parse font family and store it in the database (probably needs Pillow)
* Virtual font (needs better name) (12)
  * Groups one or more fonts
  * Defines per language rules (eg. use this font for CJK languages)
* Check (16)
  * Parses params
  * Loads correct font based on virtual font definition (needs custom fontconfig configuration)
  * Renders text using Pango and measures dimensions


**Additional context**
Possible renderer snippet: https://mail.python.org/pipermail/python-list/2008-December/494841.html, wrapping can be configured by https://developer.gnome.org/pygtk/stable/class-pangolayout.html#method-pangolayout--set-wrap

summary: Add a configuration option to make the translation length limit based on the source string optional
description:
Use case:

When translating language files which are key value based with short keys like "home.description" and a long translation Weblate currently limits the length of the translation to max(100, source.length * 10), in this example 160 chars. To avoid adding a manual max-length constraint to all keys tapping into this case the option LIMIT_TRANSLATION_LENGTH_BY_SOURCE_LENGTH can be set to false. If it's set to false the calculation will be skipped and instead translations up to 10.000 characters are allowed.

summary: Better handling of BCP 47 language tags
description:
The translation files in my repository use BCP 47 language tags (e.g. `en-AU`). If I use the **Start New Translation** feature and pick one of the standard languages, the translation is added using the POSIX format (e.g. `en_AU`) as per the language definition in Weblate, which is not suitable for my repository.

I have tried using the administration interface to modify the language definitions to use BCP 47 instead. Although this fixes the problem, when Weblate restarts it automatically creates the standard language definitions in POSIX format, effectively duplicating the BCP 47 ones. (I am running Weblate in Docker.) I do not want these POSIX ones to be available when using the **Start New Translation** feature.

The best solution that I can think of would be to add a setting that tells Weblate to set up the standard languages using the BCP 47 format.

I've considered changing my repository to use POSIX format, but it uses private use subtags (e.g. `en-AU-x-test`) and there does not seem to be a standard way to represent these in POSIX format.

description:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
It does not appear to be currently possible to create a new language in the front end. Only in the django administration. We have users that should be able to create new languages but should not be able to log into the django administration. Previously it was possible to limit permissions in the django administration but that is no longer possible since weblate has its own permissions table `weblate_auth_user` now.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Add back possibity to give permissions to weblate users to access only parts of the django administration.

summary: Return a Last-Modified header for translation downloads
description:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
We're using Drupal to automatically download translations from Weblate as PO files. In order to minimise file downloads Drupal first performs a HEAD request for the PO file and will only actually download the file when a Last-Modified header is present that gives a date that is newer than the last download time.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
The `/download/[project]/[component]/[language]` URL should provide the Last-Modified header with a timestamp that is set to the value of the last change made to the component for that language (similar to what is displayed in the user interface).

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Hardcoding this header to a value far in the future on the server level. This has some obvious drawbacks as it may break in a few hundred years, however, it's also wasteful in having to download the translations during each check.

**Additional context**

summary: Possibility to export project data in xml ldml format
description:
**Describe the solution you'd like**
We already have the possibility to export the translation files of the projects in many formats (CSV, MO, PO, TBX, TMX, XLIFF and XLSX), but since there are some projects with data that could be imported in the Unicode CLDR survey tool (for example, all the ISO locale data for Debian), it would be really useful to translators that already worked on those to be able to download the files in the LDML XML format that Unicode uses ( http://unicode.org/reports/tr35/ ).

Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Create a source locale with plural translations containing one/other
2. Create another locale, such as AR that supports two/many/few/zero
3. No option to translate two/many/few/zero is available

**Expected behavior**
I'd expect to be able to translate those plurals

**Additional context**
I have no access directly to the weblate installation to give more details about configuration, but I can try to spin up a docker installation to test if needed.

summary: Move push on commit to background
description:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Offload push to celery task

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Current approach takes to too long requests in some cases without any benefit.

summary: Non-git based components
description: We have translatable content that is not tied to code, for example CMS-style content and email campaign content. Since weblate is a really good tool to handle translations, and are translators have experience with it we would like to use weblate to handle translations instead of trying to replicate parts of it. Currently we are doing that by automatically managing a git repository with a copy of our content, essentially doing a data-export on every change, and re-importing when we receive a webhook from github/bitbucket. I am wondering if it is possible to take out the git part of this? For example use a weblate API to directly push texts to weblate, along with a webhook from weblate so we can automatically receive updated translations or mark content as unusable if a translators flags text as needing review.

4. Run `./manage.py updategit --all`

**Expected behavior**

summary: Faster consistency check on import
description:
On importing of big projects, quite a lot of time is spent on the consistency checks. It seems to be good idea to perform this check just once at the end of component import using single SQL query:

```python
        Unit.objects.filter(
            translation__component__project=project,
            translation__component__allow_translation_propagation=True,
        ).values(
            'content_hash', 'translation__language'
        ).annotate(
            Count('target', distinct=True)
        ).filter(
            target__count__gt=1
        )
```

This way whole work is offloaded to the SQL server and it seems to perform way better than doing this per unit while importing.

summary: Configurable language names when creating translations
description:
This is mostly a question, to clarify some details regarding language tags. Languages on disk are saved with the posix language format like  `en_US` instead of the language tag format used in web and all new modern tools `en-us`. 

Can we switch to this format. This is also to establish a common format since new added languages are added with the language tag. 
Example: 

We have some translations that cover a specific region of the world like: Eastern Africa. 
According to the language tag specification [1], I can define a language specific to that region like `ar-014` [2].  

I've defined such a language and it seem to work after I put in the proper plurals (manually copied from arabic).


[1] https://www.w3.org/International/articles/language-tags/ 
[2] https://www.iana.org/assignments/language-subtag-registry/language-subtag-registry

```
Type: region
Subtag: 014
Description: Eastern Africa
Added: 2005-10-16
```

summary: Disable punctuation checks for Lojban
description:

- `EndStopCheck`
- `EndColonCheck`
- `EndQuestionCheck`
- `EndExclamationCheck`
- `EndEllipsisCheck`

The furthest date for dropping support Django 1.11 is upstream support and it is supported [until at least April 2020](https://www.djangoproject.com/download/#supported-versions).

We are using the `xcodebuild` CLI tool in order to export our strings into `xliff` format. Since Xcode 9.3 Apple changed something which results in having new lines as `\n` instead of new line characters and I couldn't find a way to adjust that behavior.

So the example string "Test1\nTest2" resulted in a xliff format like this:

```
      <trans-unit id="Test">
        <source>Test1
Test2</source>
      </trans-unit>
```

... and now like this:

Weblate *does* show new line characters for the first example, but only shows `\n` for the second.

We don't want our translators to have to take care of adding `\n` for new lines, we just want them to hit enter for new lines, just like before.

Is there a way to have `\n` in the .xliff files while showing new line characters in Weblate? Also, new target translations done using the enter key also have to be saved as `\n` behind the scenes then.

I guess this is regarding translate-toolkit, right?

Thanks

summary: Asynchronous tasks
description:
Weblate really needs some standard way to perform tasks asynchronously in background.

Use cases:

- Fulltext index updates, currently done by queuing updates in the database and executing by cron
- Processing update hooks, currently done by forking thread to do the update
- Translation memory updates, see https://github.com/WeblateOrg/weblate/issues/1919
- Email sending, see https://github.com/WeblateOrg/weblate/issues/492 and https://github.com/WeblateOrg/weblate/issues/1046

Ideal solution would have:

- Django integration
- Rollbar integration (alternatively we might switch to self hosted Sentry)
- Scheduled tasks to perform maintenance and send digest mails
- Batch tasks to allow effective updates of Whoosh indexes (translation memory and fulltext search)
- Redis is preferred backend (database doesn't work for us as IndexUpdate table has locking issues right now)

Possible candidates:

- [TaskTiger](https://github.com/closeio/tasktiger) - lacks Django integration
- [RQ](http://python-rq.org/) and [Django RQ](https://github.com/ui/django-rq) - lacks Rollbar integration and batch updates
- [Celery](http://www.celeryproject.org/) - supports Django, lacks batch tasks, there is way to [integrate with Rollbar](https://www.mattlayman.com/blog/2017/django-celery-rollbar/)

Other suggestions welcome!

summary: Push translations to the translation memory
description:
There should be way to feed [built in translation memory](https://docs.weblate.org/en/latest/admin/memory.html) with strings translated in Weblate. This needs to handle several situations:

- Sitewide installation, when all strings are pushed to TM, this is usually desired in the installation used by single company.
- Per project or component installation (maybe it could utilize addons) for multi purpose installation such as Hosted Weblate. By installing enabling TM addon, users will get access to it and all their translations will go there. This probably needs some legal framework as well.

The updates should be batched and run in the background. We could reuse code for fulltext index updates, but maybe it's just better to switch to some task queue (which we need anyway, see https://github.com/WeblateOrg/weblate/issues/492). So far I think the best match would be https://github.com/closeio/tasktiger as it supports batching requests, what is perfect fit for translation memory or index updates.

summary: Replace GroupACL with something more reasonable [$50 awarded]
description:
While the GroupACL is certainly better than having just group based access Django provides, it turns out to be pretty hard to configure properly due to permission filtering and layering of GroupACLs. Also the logic to evaluate this is unnecessarily complex.

**Summary of this is available in the wiki: https://github.com/WeblateOrg/weblate/wiki/Access-control-design**

Problems with current GroupACL:

* Unclear layering of them, it's pretty much coded here, but ordering within same group is pretty much random:

https://github.com/WeblateOrg/weblate/blob/90c2d8edcff1c984f3d953fe29f0e9a927b2feaf/weblate/permissions/helpers.py#L61-L71

* The idea of permissions filtering is usually to complex to setup
* Exposing all permissions in the admin interface adds unnecessary complexity as most of the automatically generated Django permissions are not used
* The can_access permission can not be used with per language ACL as it's only applied to the translation (leading to confusing situations that user can not access /project/foo/ but can access /project/foo/bar/cs/)
* The project and language ACL does not seem to work (this might be just bug in the current implementation)

We probably should focus on creating something simple which will cover most of the use cases and then potentially extend it.

What we need from the access control system:

* Define access to individual projects, translations or languages (not sure about components)
* Granular permissions (access project, translate, suggest, review, ...)
* Interface to edit per project groups directly in Weblate
* Automatic adding of users to groups

What can be probably omitted from current feature:

* Restrict access by additional rules (currently GroupACL can be used to revoke permissions)
* Defining permissions for individual users, having groups is good enough in most cases

Following use cases should work (some of them might be duplicate, but that's real world situations I've met so far):

* Grant every user translation permission to a project
* Grant project visibility to group only
* Grant group review permission to a language in all projects
* Grant group translation permission to a language in all projects
* Grant group translation permission to a language in single project
* Grant admin access to a project to a group

[![Bountysource](https://api.bountysource.com/badge/issue?issue_id=53891719)](https://www.bountysource.com/issues/53891719-replace-groupacl-with-something-more-reasonable?utm_source=53891719&utm_medium=shield&utm_campaign=ISSUE_BADGE)

summary: Wrong history shown on git merge
description:
### Steps to reproduce
1. Let Weblate create merge commit.
2. Look at it on GitHub (or other tool which shows diff for merge commit)

### Actual behaviour

The diff in upstream changes is shown, for example:
https://github.com/WeblateOrg/weblate/commit/4e50b8ce278989d85b5a2560e13c8d3ea691e36b


### Expected behaviour

The diff with Weblate changes should be shown.

### The problem

All tools seem to use the second parent as branch to show diff, so Weblate should create the merge commit in reverse order. However there seems to be no way to tell git to do this.

As a workaround Weblate could do following:

```
# Create local branch for upstream
git branch tmp origin/master
# Checkout upstream branch
git checkout tmp
# Merge current Weblate changes, this can lead to conflict
git merge master
# Checkout branch with Weblate changes
git checkout master
# Merge temporary branch (this is fast forward so does not create merge commit)
git merge tmp
# Delete temporary branch
git branch -d tmp
```
As this involves quite a lot of manipulations with the repository, it can lead to performance issues. Also this really looks too complex for simple thing we want to achieve.

PS: Asked this question on [StackOverflow](https://stackoverflow.com/q/48302475/225718).

summary: Automatic creation/deletion of Components

We work with a Git-Flow approach, having short living feature-branches which get merged back into development branch after review, testing and translating.

After evaluating Weblate (dockerized setup) for our needs, it remains still unclear how we would implement automatic Component creation (for new feature-branches) in the most efficient way.

It is tedious to set up a new component in the Web-UI for every feature-branch we start working on, so we are looking for a way to automate this.

Unfortunately the WEB-API doesn't allow to create components (https://github.com/WeblateOrg/weblate/issues/1225). What is the reason behind this?

Github Web-Hooks can only be used to update components, but won't create new ones.

The only achievable way we found is to use manage.py (rsp. weblate alias in docker container) to create components via "import_json" command. "import_project" does not work for us, since it has too few configuration options.

Using manage.py to automatically create components looks a little strange to us. Needing to have our CI-Server to call Weblate via SSH to execute configuration within a named docker-container isn't the most elegant solution to go with.

Did we overlook something? Might there be a better way to achieve this? If not, are there plans to implement component-creation/deletion in a different way?

Thanks.

summary: Offline Description Column in CSV
description:
Hello,

One of the challenges we're facing is being able to export descriptions into CSV's and being able to import them back into Weblate. 
I've seen the following relevant issues:

1. https://github.com/WeblateOrg/weblate/issues/407
2. https://github.com/WeblateOrg/weblate/issues/772
3. https://github.com/WeblateOrg/weblate/issues/1194

I understand the complications that would be involved in exporting and merging back in changes to comments.
An alternative solution that might remedy this complication might be to add a new field into the Weblate interface: "Description". The data here would persist in the Weblate database, but could also be exported into the CSV and imported back in to update the database. 

This solution would allow developers and an internal product team to collaborate on a solid description-- such as, discuss via the comments of Weblate, and then agree on description field. Then, they could export the CSV, which would include the description column for translators to be able to view offline.


Our team has a working proof of concept of this idea. However, we are concerned about maintaining it internally across Weblate upgrades. We were wondering about the feasibility of including this as a feature in Weblate-- that could perhaps be enabled in the admin interface with an explanation of its function in CSV import/exports.

What do you think?

summary: Homepage for new users displays all projects in all languages
description:
in `trans/views/basic.py`, function `get_user_translations` for unauthenticated users filters list of translation by session language. Unless that language is english.

This means that browsers that prefer english will load all translations for all languages.

Unfortunately, this query is the base for all the homepage queries. In conjunction with component list feature, this can mean that unauthenticated user is loading a page listing potentially _all languages for all components_ that are in some component list -- initially hidden from view behind the component list switches.

On l10n.opensuse.org, this results in a 23MB homepage that actually times out on the outbound proxy.

A quick fix we're using is removing the `and session_lang != "en"` part of the filter.
Part of the proper solution would be on-demand loading of component lists. Another part would be reviewing the `get_user_translations` function and its usages for sanity, because the logic it uses now is a little weird ;) and not appropriate as a base query for the other queries in `home()`.

summary: Plural support in JSON files [$50 awarded]
description:
I find myself needing plural support in JSON format. I am pretty flexible about which toolkit to use, so I don't quite care if that uses i18next or MessageFormat format. 

The [i18next syntax](https://www.i18next.com/plurals.html) is the simplest of the two and looks like this:

```json
{
   "key": "You have {{count}} item.",
   "key_plural": "You have {{count}} items"
}
```

For languages with multiple plural forms the key format is `key_#` for fixed-number strings, and `key_plural` for other numbers. 

The [ICU MessageFormat format](https://formatjs.io/guides/message-syntax/) is more powerful, and thus more complex. While it is interesting, I expect it would require a massive UI change to support properly.

@nijel  I'm happy to set a bounty for this. Can you give an indication of what would be needed?

summary: support Google Play upload tools: Fastlane and Triple-T Gradle Play Publisher
description:
There are two major tools for managing the localized files for Google Play:  Fastlane Supply and Triple-T Gradle Play Publisher.  F-Droid also supports the same file/dir structure.  If Weblate would directly support those files, then there would be a clean, simple, automated way to translate Android apps using Weblate. Here's the ideal workflow:

1. Weblate pulls source from git
2. translators work in Weblate
3. translations get pulled into app's source directly where Fastlane or Triple-T expect them
4. F-Droid automatically uses those translations from git
5. those translations are directly published to Google Play via the respective tool (Fastlane Supply or Gradle)

Both Fastlane and Triple-T use plain text for the source and translation file format.  _title_ and _short_description_ would be easy to support directly as plain text, _changelog_ and _full_description_ much less so:

* _title_: 30 char limit, one line, plain text
* _short_description_: 80 char limit, one line, plain text
*  _full_description_: 4000 char limit, multiple lines, can contain basic HTML
* _changelog_: 500 char limit, multiple lines, plain text

But perhaps this setup is just too different from standard translation workflows that assume strings are in a single source file.  I've also opened issues on those tools to get feedback there:
* https://github.com/Triple-T/gradle-play-publisher/issues/227
* https://github.com/fastlane/fastlane/issues/9520

I really want to find a way to get this workflow working really smoothly.  Translations are really important, and something that really should be as automated as possible.

This might be very similar to #197, but given its complexity this could be an alternative for shorter term consideration.

Right now if someone edits a non-source language (lets say "fr-FR" for french), the source string is shown regardless and has a little pencil for "Edit source string" next to it. Clicking that one navigates to the source language (lets say "en-GB" for english).

It would be nice if there were a dropdown somewhere that lets the user pick one of the languages currently present in the project/component, so they can switch from en-GB to fr-FR to de-AT to whatever other language they'd like to look at.
Main reason I'd like to see a feature like that is because the URL is not interchangable (which looks like `/translate/Proj/Comp/en-GB/?sid=<guid>`); I cannot simply replace "en-GB" with "fr-FR" in the URL and end up in the other language (but the same resource key).

And as a scaled down version of that, alternatively, we could use secondary languages (which right now are shown as read-only) and put a small pencil next to them as well (with the same functionality as "Edit source string", except they go to the given language instead).
I imagine this to be easier, because the "Edit source string" URL looks different and _is_ interchangable (which looks like `/translate/Proj/Comp/en-GB/?checksum=<hash>`) between languages.

summary: Translation-time context management

Edit: see [comment](https://github.com/WeblateOrg/weblate/issues/1507#issuecomment-351581732) for clarification.


Hi. Is it possible to add a option for translators to manage msgctxts, including adding new ones?

I'm not sure if that's something needed or even viable, so let me describe the situation first:
* There's a translation going from a gender unspecific language (English) to a gender specific one (Spanish). Most strings are common, but some, maybe 10-15% will differ.
* The translation will result in 2 separate packages, male and female
* I could create a common project and two separate components. But I'll have to disable translation propagation, because otherwise they'll mess up each other strings.
* And without propagation, looks like the only way to share the effort is to copy the strings manually. (Or maybe "copy and save" from machine translation tab, will it appear there? Still, that would be a lot of clicking and manual coordination between components)
* The key problem is that in the source, it's not known beforehand whether the string is gender specific or not. That is decided by the translator at the time of translation, on a case by case basis. (and may vary for different languages, too)

So... that looks like a long shot, but I was thinking of a feature that would allow the translator to "split" the source string into several contexted ones and translate them individually? That will require adding newly created entries into po and pot, though.

Or maybe I'm missing an obvious way to handle such a situation? Please advise.

summary: Suggestion to enhance FAQ How to fix merge conflicts in translations?
description:
The FAQ *How to fix merge conflicts in translations?* documents generic git conflict merge. In case of Gettext po files, "edit" is not a smart way to do it. gettext-tools can do it better.

In addition to the generic merge, it would be nice to document Gettext po specific way to merge conflicts:

1. Clone the whole set of commands in the frame.

2. Add text:

*In case of Gettext po files, there is a way to merge conflict in a semi-automatic way:*

*Get and keep local clone of the Weblate git repository. Also get a second fresh local clone of the upstream git repository (i. e. you need two copies of the upstream git repository: intact and working copy).*

3. And it the Gettext po specific frame, change:

```shell
# Add remote
git remote add weblate https://hosted.weblate.org/git/weblate/master/
```

change to

```shell
# Add remote
git remote add weblate /path/to/weblate/snapshot/
```

```shell
# Resolve conflicts
edit ....
git add ...
```

```shell
# Resolve conflicts
for PO in space separated list of conflicting po files ; do
	msgcat --use-first /path/to/weblate/snapshot/$PO\
			   /path/to/upstream/snapshot/$PO -o $PO.merge
	msgmerge --previous --lang=${PO%.po} $PO.merge domain.pot -o $PO
	rm $PO.merge
	git add $PO
done
```

description:

The caching has to stay in order to have consistent view when translating (once you filter not translated strings, you want to be able to navigate through it even if you have translated something meanwhile).

* If the URL contains search parameters, new search is performed and stored in session cache, further only the search_id is used in the URLs.

We can most likely identify the session cache directly by parameters thus avoid need to exposing some internals in the URL.

summary: Migrate project membership to Group ACL

There is currently no real reason to have two modifications to permissions - project membership and ownership and Group ACL. Group ACL is clearly superior and can be used to implement project membership and ownership.

* Automatically create defined set of groups for each ACL enanabled project (tentatively `Project: Developers`)
* Adjust management code to add users to correct groups instead of adding owner or to per project group
* Migrate existing ownership and membership data to Group ACL
* Remove the ownership relation as that will be now handle using Group ACL
* Whenever generic groups are updated, update the per project ones to ease managing permissions (probably this should be configurable)

This will allow us to add more permission levels in project ACL management (eg. add additional group for Git repository access)

summary: Reconsider checksums usage
description:
Currently we use md5 and char(32) fields to speed up strings lookup. This works well for long strings, but for short ones it is not that beneficial as the lookup costs about same as the actual string lookup.

Maybe it would be better to use some shorter hash (we really don't care that much about collisions for lookups) and store the value as integer in the database.

Things to consider:

* Which hash function to use? [SipHash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SipHash) seems to be option, though the pure Python implementation will probably lack desired performance. There is [csiphash](https://github.com/zacharyvoase/python-csiphash) though.
* Storing in [BigIntegerField](https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/1.10/ref/models/fields/#bigintegerfield) is possible since Django 1.10.
* Migration path would mean that all units in the database are updated, what would be quite slow migration. The benefits really have to outweigh this.

summary: Needs review and fuzzy confusion
description:
Since 91895e53843ba541750e2c827fa15babd8bfff43 we label "fuzzy" strings as marked for review. This was probably not a good move as it adds further level of confusion. Some feedback I got:

> Could you consider adding a note next to the 'needs review' checkbox, indicating that 'needs review' also necessarily means that for all practical purposes, such messages are considered untranslated. I.e. the program will not use them.
> 
> Currently, translators may think of 'needs review' as an administrative setting, for personal use or communication with other translators, and without further consequences. And then wonder why their hard work doesn't end up in their favorite program...

What we probably need is separate flags for following situations:

* The string was fuzzy matched and needs proper translation
* The string needs review, but is properly translated

Mapping these two should be different based on file format:

* Gettext `fuzzy` should be flagged as `fuzzy matched`
* Qt TS `unfinished` should be flagged as `fuzzy matched`
* XLIFF without `approved="yes"` should get into `needs review`

summary: Fallback groups for GroupACL
description:
I expected this to be necessary, so this issue is mostly for record keeping.

If #1070 gets fixed, we will have no way to allow users _any_ actions on GroupACL-locked objects, unless we add a "fallback group".

That is, change behavior of GroupACL locking from:
1. if you're member of a locked group, you get permissions from the group
2. otherwise, you don't get any permissions whatsoever

to:

1. if you're member of a locked group, you get permissions from the group
2. otherwise, you get permissions from a designated "fallback" group

The expected usecase would be to designate a group -- either use Guests, or pared-down Users (#1069 for copying or inheriting groups) -- with "lower than usual" permissions.

A potential issue is with anonymous/known users distinction. With the fallback mechanism, we would either grant both logged-in and anonymous users the same privileges, or we would lock out anonymous users completely.
Alternately, we could add an "anonymous fallback", which seems excessive. Or, possibly most reasonable, limit anonymous users to those permissions that they get from Guests and that are present on the fallback group at the same time.
(so for example, if Guests `can_suggest` and FallbackGroup also `can_suggest`, anonymous users can post suggestions. However, if Guests can suggest and FallbackGroup can't, anonymous users can't suggest either)
Maybe this behavior should apply to the fallback group in general? Name it "retain group" and consider the group a set of permissions that you retain if you got them from the result of `user.has_perm`.

what do you think?

summary: Improvements for translation page UX
description:
Basically we in the near future would like weblate to become our "translation community". Right now we use a lot of files to communicate with our translators, and to explain them the context about a translation. What we would like to see could be a quick-fix to drastically improve translation interaction:
1. While translating, make 'comments' the tab that is selected by default. Right now that is 'nearby messages', which is a bit less useful. Maybe comments always should be visible, and the tabs should be shown #1058
2. Also add the number of nearby messages in the header (as with suggestions) #1059
3. What does the comment scope do? It only shows the gray label at the right of the comment? Do not think people understand that, we think it should always be 'translation comment' right? Would make this a simple toggle next to the 'save' button, or maybe remove it? #1060
4. The location of the 'search' tab is a bit odd, it is not related to that translation string right? Would expect it to be in the page header. We would like to use the search all day if we want to do ad-hoc translations. #1061
5. Let all 'save' buttons float right? People are right action oriented. #1062
6. There is no button to exit 'Zen edit mode'? #1063

Hope you like my positive criticism :+1: The translating experience should be as smooth as possible.

summary: Integrate Git repositories export
description:
Manually exporting Git repositories is painful and maintaining ACL for that is easy cause for errors.

Therefore we should have integrated support for exporting git repos. This will be optional as it probably can be universal enough.

Components to use:
- nginx will handle authentication via requests to weblate - http://nginx.org/en/docs/http/ngx_http_auth_request_module.html
- gitolite to handle per repository access - http://gitolite.com/gitolite/gitolite.html#http

Needed steps:
- [ ] Hook into component manipulations to export repos
- [ ] Hook into permissions to export ACLs to gitolite
- [ ] Write exported repository path to component
- [ ] Implement authentication callback (maybe we could reuse something from API, see #416).

The translations are marked as "need review".

summary: Punctuation for Bodo (brx)
description:
Could Devanagari punctuation be added for `brx` and possibly other languages which use Devnagari? The buttons are only showing English punctuation and other special characters for me (en_GB.UTF-8).

I've noticed that in the absence of nice punctuation buttons, our translator(s) sometimes use `U+007C | vertical line` in place of [danda or doublle danda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danda). See https://hosted.weblate.org/translate/mypaint/mypaint/brx/?checksum=2c56907bc6cb3516dbf2eb5ec1548bed. Because this is happening, sometimes the trailing stop check is triggered at times when the translator has written something that must read correctly to them: https://hosted.weblate.org/translate/mypaint/mypaint/brx/?type=allchecks.

This may just be a case of the correct script not being associated with the language.

It may be a good idea to allow `|` for `।`, and `||` for `॥`, but I can't read or write Devanagari - I'm not sure how much of a hack this would be.

I think this will save us huge amount of time creating a custom tool to workaround the problem.

summary: Lithuanian lokalization projects may use both 3 and 4 plural forms
description:
Some localization projects of Lithuanian use 3 plural forms, while others use 4 forms (e.g. KDE, openSUSE team)

Reasons:
- Historically Lithuanian in software localization had 3 plural forms:
  - 1, 21, 31, 41, 51...
  - 22, 23, 24... 29, 32... 39, 42...49, 52... 59...
  - 11, 12, 13... 19, 29, 30, 40, 50, 60...
- Arises problem while translating really single 1, because in Lithuanian the same ruler apllay for "1 atnaujinimas" ("1 update") and "21 atnaujinimas" ("21 updates") (and its OK, if there is number "%d atnaujinimas", where %d = 1 or 21 ), but there is error to say "update" for 1 and "update" for 21 (both in Lithuanian, and in English). So some localization teams decided to switch to 4 plural forms to make distinction between 1 and x1 (21, 31...)

Lithuanian KDE team switched in 2009 (if you could read in Lithuanian...):
https://mail.kde.org/pipermail/kde-i18n-lt/2009-September/000324.html
http://kde.akl.lt/?p=148

For openSUSE project transition from 3 to 4 plurals was done in 2010 (in English message):
http://lists.opensuse.org/opensuse-translation/2010-08/msg00001.html

See some discussion in English: https://bugs.launchpad.net/ubuntu/+source/language-pack-kde-lt/+bug/565294

The similar situation was with other languages, like Serbian, Hebrew...

So Webplate should be compatible to both variants of Lithuanian language, at first it should respect plural forms determined in header of PO file.

summary: add support for new language hooks
description:
Adding a new translations now could requite an additional manual work.

However there are many ways to update languages list, adding a support for several of them will cover major part of Open Source projects. It would be nice to make possible to add hooks for them, so Weblate could add new languages automatically.

Here is the list of basic hooks:
- file named LINGUAS in the translations directory
- file named LINGUAS in po directory (in such case, all translation subprojects needs to have the same list of existing translations)
- line starting with ALL_LINGUAS= in configure.ac, configure.in (and configure, if it exists in the git repo) (in such case, all translation subprojects needs to have the same list of existing translations)

In general, the hook inputs should be:
- the source tree itself
- list of all existing languages
- the language that is being added
- list of other sub-projects that operate on the same tree (e. g. two directories po, po-locations with ALL_LINGUAS method imply, that adding of translation to po will require adding a file to po-locations).

The output would be a list of files that were changed or added.

Here is a shell hook I successfully use in the SUSE translation-update-upstream project (cwd is a directory with po files, OLDPWD is a top directory of the project, LNG is the name of language being added). This hook is not good enough for Weblate, as it adds languages unsorted.

``` shell
# Update all known mechanisms to add language:
function linguas_update {
    if test -f LINGUAS -o -f ../po/LINGUAS ; then
        if test -f LINGUAS ; then
        if sed '/^#/d' <LINGUAS | grep -q '[a-zA-Z0-9] [a-z]' ; then
            echo "Adding $LNG to LINGUAS in to a list in single-line list mode."
            sed -i "s/^[^#].* [a-z].*\$/& $LNG/" LINGUAS
        else
            echo "Adding $LNG to LINGUAS."
            echo $LNG >>LINGUAS
        fi
        else
        echo "Not adding $LNG to LINGUAS - secondary domain, global LINGUAS."
        fi
    else
        if test -f $OLDPWD/configure.ac ; then
        if grep -q 'ALL_LINGUAS=' $OLDPWD/configure.ac ; then
            echo "Adding $LNG to configure.ac."
            sed -i 's/ALL_LINGUAS="/&'$LNG' /;s/\(ALL_LINGUAS=\)\([^"]\|$\)/\1"'$LNG' "\2/' $OLDPWD/configure.ac
        fi
        fi
        if test -f $OLDPWD/configure.in ; then
        if grep -q 'ALL_LINGUAS=' $OLDPWD/configure.in ; then
            echo "Adding $LNG to configure.in."
            sed -i 's/ALL_LINGUAS="/&'$LNG' /;s/\(ALL_LINGUAS=\)\([^"]\|$\)/\1"'$LNG' "\2/' $OLDPWD/configure.in
        fi
        fi
        if test -f $OLDPWD/configure ; then
        if grep -q 'ALL_LINGUAS=' $OLDPWD/configure ; then
            echo "Adding $LNG to configure."
            sed -i 's/ALL_LINGUAS="/&'$LNG' /;s/\(ALL_LINGUAS=\)\([^"]\|$\)/\1"'$LNG' "\2/' $OLDPWD/configure
        fi
        fi
    fi
}
```

summary: Checks can be disabled by default
description:
Adds a `default_disabled` field to the `Check` class which can be set to disable a check by default. This generalizes the current implementation for the format checks and allows custom checks that are disabled by default but can be explicitly enabled using the proper flag.

This can be used in custom checks as follows:

```
class FooCheck(TargetCheck):

    check_id = 'foo'
    name = _('Foo check')
    description = _('Your translation is foo')
    default_disabled = True

    # Real check code
    def check_single(self, source, target, unit, cache_slot):
        return 'foo' in target
```

If this checks gets included it will not be run by default, but one can explicitly set the `foo` tag for a unit. The existing checks in weblate/trans/checks/format.py have been migrated to use this new functionality.

I will write some tests for my own use using this functionality and if the tests have a wider use I will provide pull requests for them, too.

summary: Newline marker (↵) can be copied into translations

One way this could be prevented is by inserting the character not into the HTML, but using CSS like `.nl:before { content: "\21b5"; }`. Such text (at least in the Epiphany browser) does not get copied in the clipboard.

It would be great to be abe to hide-unhide the completed translations when i am a translator.

summary: enhancement: Commit this file
description:
It would be great to be able to commit one specific file to the repo, even maybe changing the commit message. 
Currently I can only commit all the changes at once, but my idea is to create a cleaner git log and just commit big changes, letting one liners for next commit if possible.

description:
Hello:

summary: Optimize repository status
description:
When showing repository status, it should exclude linked repos, so that every repo is listed just once.

For example https://hosted.weblate.org/projects/noosfero/#repository shows huge page with repository status, but in fact here is just one underlaying repository.

description:

It would be great if there was a link to jump to the source where I can fix the typo.

description:

Base file for new translations is not used because of project settings.

summary: Subproject.branch default value is master
description:
When I tried to set a test instance up with Mercurial, the first thing I bumped into was that the default value for the branch is set to "master". I suppose this works with Git, but with Mercurial I bump into configure_branch in vcs.py that complains that the branch must be "default". Took a while to figure out that one of the fields I hadn't touched had an incompatible default value.

Perhaps you could use use empty string as default and treat it specially, or treat "default" specially for git? If you aren't already, I suppose this could just be a bug. :)

Another thing that I couldn't figure out initially is that the intro docs talks about creating a component, but the model is actually subproject.

Otherwise, thanks for Weblate, it's awesome!

summary: Support Chrome JSON translations
description:
Currently Weblate supports simple key:value (both mono- or bi-lingual) translation for JSON.

However there are some more complex formats in the wild providing some more information to the translators, for example JSON used for Chrome extensionts: https://github.com/FelisCatus/SwitchyOmega/blob/master/omega-i18n/en/messages.json

Weblate should support this as well, but probably translate-toolkit support is needed first.

This was originally also tracked in #627, but I think it's better to track separately.

summary: Automate hosting requests
description:
The hosting requests for https://hosted.weblate.org/ should be automated.
- user has to be logged in first
- user submits project information along with repository URL
- weblate scans it (git ls-remote,...) finds suitable translation files and calculates mask (#32)
- once everything is ready it's submitted for approval
- on approval all needed models are created

The intermediate data should be stored in separate table (maybe as JSON data) and the real models are created only after approval.

summary: Add support for Localized Property List File (OS X >= 10.9 and iOS >= 7)
description:
Hi guys,

In the past days i successfully set up weblate for a big iOS project.
Now i'm trying to figuring out how to properly manage plurals and genders using Weblate.

Some time ago [Apple introduced "Localized property list file"](https://developer.apple.com/library/ios/releasenotes/Foundation/RN-Foundation/#//apple_ref/doc/uid/TP30000742-CH2-SW56).

You can find more [here](https://developer.apple.com/library/ios/documentation/General/Reference/InfoPlistKeyReference/Articles/AboutInformationPropertyListFiles.html) and another explanations [here](https://github.com/objcio/articles/blob/master/2014-02-10-string-localization.md#plural-and-gender-support).

Any future plan to support this?

Thanks

summary: Properly use static files framework in Django
description:
Weblate currently still uses MEDIA dirs to serve it's static files. This was true in some ancient Django version and we should really switch to static files usage. That would also make our setup much more standard.

The data files could be by default collected in DATA_DIR as defined in #604.

summary: Consolidate filesystem paths
description:
Currently Weblate has too many filesystem paths which need to be configured, let's simplify that, all data should go to single directory, that includes:
- vcs repositories (currently in GIT_ROOT)
- whoosh index (currently in WHOOSH_INDEX)
- avatar cache (configured in CACHE)
- ssh keys, known hosts and wrapper (currently in HOME)

There should be single setting (eg. DATA_DIR) and all other will be automatically stored under it.

summary: “Not translated” quality check too picky
description:
I notice that when the translation of a string is equal to the source it is "tagged" as “Not translated”.

I think it would be better to not do that, or at least give an option to "relax" that kind of check that considers as “Not translated” only the entries where the translation is effectively missing.

The rationale is that there are obviously legitimate cases for that:
- the original word is a technical term, that may have no correspondence, or it is in widespread use in the target language (think at _computer_ for example)
- it is a _foreign_ word also in the source language (for example, the Latin _idem_ word)

summary: weblate doesn't work with Django 1.7

summary: Properties file translation repository browser location
description:
Currently when using the suggested parameters in the repository browser url with Java Properties translation format, the only working variable is the %(branch)s, as:
(changes suggested in trans/models/unit.py:get_location_links)
- %(file)s is the identifier of the string, which is not the filename in case of Java Properties. Digging deeper, the location of the translation unit is the same as the context of the translation unit (the identifier of the string to translate from the properties file). A better value for the file parameter for this format would be self.translation.filename
- %(line)s is always 0, a better approximation (although not perfect because of the empty lines) would be self.position for this format

summary: Add rebase option to UI
description: Admin should be able to do git rebase from UI to get rid of extra merge commits.

summary: Clear environment for external commands
description:
In light of CVE-2014-6271 we should do environment cleanup before executing external commands.

Note that Weblate does not directly call bash, but it can be called by git hooks or in helper scripts.

summary: Change "source" suggestion.
description:
Hi, I'd like to implement a feature for a translator to suggest a new English source string.

What would the best approach be to implement this? Could you describe maybe short what to do?

My intuition tells me to implement it similar to the "comment" feature, and create a table like "Comment" (but without the language field.)

Then, when new PO files are imported through git, and we notice that the new source is there. (Because the translator changed the source string.), then we can remove this suggestion, but maybe apply the translations already.

summary: Include repository URL in merge failure mail
description: When sending merge failure notification, URL of exported git repo should be included (if that is available) so that user can directly try merge.

summary: Any example for gitolite access?
description:
Hello,
This is more support-request, I think, but I found not better place to put it.
I would like to use Weblate with gitolite-hosted Git repository.
Is that possible?
I've specified git repository like "git@myserver:myrepo" and put Weblate-generated keys into gitolite, but I get error on creating subproject:

`Failed to fetch git repository: 'git remote update origin' returned exit status 1: Host key verification failed. fatal: The remote end hung up unexpectedly error: Could not fetch origin`

Did anybody succeeded to use Weblate with gitolite? I would be very grateful for any hints.

summary: Make email verification work without sessions
description: Currently email verification (for both registration and password reset) relies on storing registration data (email) in the session. This obviously fails if user confirms from another browser or if session has timed out meanwhile.

summary: Add support for explicit DCO
description:
Some project require contributions to be Signed-Off-By with accompanying DCO. Weblate should provide support for this:
- Add UI for accepting DCO
- Properly signoff commits
- Avoid contributions without agreeing to DCO
##

summary: Safe mode for translating web applications
description:
Some web applications could use some form of safe mode to avoid security problems with translated content.

Possible options I see right now:
- Do not allow other HTML than is in source message.
- Define set of safe markup which translators can use.
##

summary: Add support for Mercurial
description: We should really separate vcs logic from the models (see #126) and once that it done, support for other distributed VCS should be easy.

summary: Project page could use fancy progress bars as well
description: The 1.4 release improves the progress bars on the homepage to indicate texts with failing checks and fuzzy strings. It would be nice if those were shown on the progress bars for a project page as well.

summary: Auto discover github branches
description:
Add a cronjob/task that will check the github project for new branches. New branches should be added to the project automatically when the setting is enabled. The creation of the subproject (branch)  requires default settings to be provided (at project level or within settings.py file).

example of extra settings:
- SUBPROJECT_AUTO_DISCOVERY=False  # disabled by default
- SUBPROJECT_AUTO_DISCOVERY_TIME=5  # each 5 seconds
- SUBPROJECT_AUTO_DISCOVERY_EXCLUDE=  # dict of branches to exclude

or provide these settings as project settings on DB level.

summary: User management for ACL projects
description: The ACL limited projects should have some kind of control panel to add/remove users to the project without need to have full admin access.

summary: Allow to disable suggestions
description: Currently there is no way to opt out from using suggestions for particular project, but this should be possible.

summary: Make license per resource not per project
description:
Different resources can have different licensing, so it should be set per resource and not per project.

While doing this move, some other project attributes might better fit to resource ones as well (eg. adding new translation).

summary: Show project lock indicator in lists
description:
Currently user needs to start translating a project in certain language to see if it is locked currently. This is a bit late, because:
- user might want to decide to translate what isn't locked currently
- developers might want to wait for people to finish translating before building a next version of an application

Indicator could be:
- just a small padlock icon, or 
- preferably user's avatar with fallback to a small padlock icon

A list of all locks, effectively showing a group of currently active translators could be shown for:
- https://l10n.cihar.com/projects/weblate/master/ 
- https://l10n.cihar.com/projects/weblate/ 
- https://l10n.cihar.com/languages/cs/
- https://l10n.cihar.com/languages/

Some pages might require only unique users in a row, but only in extreme cases.

summary: Humanize timestamps
description:
Due to global nature of translation projects it is impossible to determine which timezone should be used for all timestamps shown in the user interface.

A better approach is to show only the most important component of time difference, eg:
- just now
- 1 minute ago
- 5 minutes ago
- 45 minutes ago
- 1 hour ago
- 18 hours ago
- 1 day ago
- 28 days ago
  ...
- 25 years ago

https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/dev/ref/contrib/humanize/#naturaltime
seems good for the purpose.

summary: Adding a new language (Qt Linguist)
description:
AFAIK, in Weblate 1.9, adding a new translation file for a subproject
using Qt Linguist ts files is not supported.

In my oppinion, the best approach to implement this would be as follows:
- Copy the base translation file.
- Replace all translated strings in the copied file with empty ones:
  <translation>foo</translation> -> <translation type="unfinished"/>
- Commit the new language file.

This approach allows the creation of an already up-to-date, empty
translation. Using this approach, there is no need to call lupdate
directly.

Another approach might be to simply create an empty ts file such
as seen in AndroidFormat [1] and commit it. The new translation file is
valid, but no source strings are available. Furthermore, there is not
enough information available to call lupdate directly from weblate (as
seen in PoFormat [2]).

What do you think? Is one of the approaches suitable or do I completely
miss the point?  I'm planning to provide you with a PR, once a good
approach for this is found.

[1] http://github.com/nijel/weblate/blob/master/weblate/trans/formats.py#L803
[2] https://github.com/nijel/weblate/blob/master/weblate/trans/formats.py#L685

PS: Originally sent by email to me, but I believe it's better to have the discussion in the issue tracker.

description:

summary: Adding secondary language in Zen mode
description:
Hello, can we add secondary language to zen mode?!

summary: Add XML validity check
description:
For the Debian Handbook, translators translate Docbook XML and they do many mistakes with the XML syntax (like mismatched tags or introducing spaces where there should be none) and it would be nice if Weblate could caught those early on.

One thing to note is that each msgid is not a valid XML tree since the englobing tag is implicit. You get "`Hello <emphasis>World</emphasis>`" and not "`<para>Hello <emphasis>World</emphasis></para>`".

And Weblate should complain if the user submits:

```
Hello <emphasis>World</ emphasis>
Hello <emphasis role = "foo">World</emphasis>
Hello <emphasis>World</emph>
```

```
    def download_translations(self, language, text, unit, user):
        '''
        Downloads list of possible translations from a service.
        '''
        url = '%s/tmserver/en/%s/unit/%s' % (
            self.url,
            urllib.quote(language),
```

summary: Do not wrap long lines?
description:
PO files generated by weblate wrap long lines.  e.g.

```
#: trans/admin_views.py:267
#, python-format
msgid ""
"Added host key for %(host)s with fingerprint %(fingerprint)s, please verify "
"that it is correct."
msgstr ""
"Clé de l'hôte ajoutée pour %(host)s avec l'empreinte %(fingerprint)s, "
"veuillez vérifier qu'elle est correcte."
```

Is it possible to disable this, e.g. like

```
msgmerge --no-wrap
```

The word-wrap makes it difficult to search for messages when using a text editor.  In this example, you cannot search for "verify that".

Also you cannot do things like this, to search for en_US spellings in en_GB files:

```
grep "^msgstr.*ize" en_GB.po
```

or this, to quickly fix typos in the source code

```
sed -i '^msgid "This is a tpyo/msgid "This is a typo' *.po
```

summary: Split checks into errors and warnings

summary: Optimize concurrent translations
description:
Currently the locks are the only way to deal with concurrent translators. 

It has a few problems:
- locking happens  only **after** first translation (i believe, didn't check)
- default lock timeout can be **too long** for shorter / trivial texts
- default lock timeout can be **too short** for longer / complex texts
- **whole** project/language is locked
- Users can unlock a project, but often don't (unless explicitly asked by other translator via some other channel)

Some improvements could be made (wild ideas):
- browsers could periodically ping (plain ajax) the server when user is actively writing to start or prolong the lock (this would allow shorter default lock)
- the lock would only lock a certain string in a language, not all strings
- in case two users have the page to translate the same string open as soon as the first one starts changing the value he gets a lock and the second user gets a notification via websockets and his input field turns readonly, or better we just disable Save button to still allow him to make suggestion, which first user gets immediately via websocket.
- both users could edit the same string, seeing other person's cursor and changes (in a dream :))

This could increase number of commits, but not necessarily if users translations are done on his own branch and merged to the original before pushing changes back to origin. Weblate "just" needs to assure there are no conflicts before merge.

All major browsers now support websocks: http://caniuse.com/#search=websocket

summary: Improve lazy commit algorithm to commit all pending changes of a given user
description:
Hi Michal,

When you use lazy commits, you obviously want to limit the number of commits appearing in the Git history. The current algorithm is not  optimal. Currently it commits the changes on a .po file as soon as someone else starts to work on it.

When this happens, it should not commit only the changes on that .po file but all the pending changes of that user, even on other files. The logic is that once you decided to create a commit for a user, you should try to put as much changes as possible in that commit.

Then I have the feeling that there's a bug that forces some commits too early, like when the same PO file of another language changes but I'm not sure. It's worth double checking though.

summary: Local, internal comment field for translator/reviewer
description:
When translating or reviewing a translation, it is often useful to provide a short, internal and non-lasting comment field.
Internal in the sense that it is only meant for translators/reviewers of the specific language.
Non-lasting in the sense that the content in the comment field is only used and kept in a short period.

The comment could be for a translator to, e.g.:
- argue why a specific translation was chosen instead of another
- refer to a source (examples where the term is used in the native language)

The reviewer would use the comment field to, e.g.:
- explain why a specific translation is not acceptable
- give suggestions on improving the translation

The current web interface for translating Debian packages [1] has a comment field like this.
It's minimalistic and simplistic in the best sense of the words.
It is a simple text field with liberal write access.
It gets wiped out as soon as the translation is committed.
Logged in users can edit the comment field - erase other users comment if no longer relevant.
I've added a screenshot [2].

The feature is part of what's nagging in Launchpad, since lack of communication between translators and reviewers stalls the translation process. An old bug report on the Launchpad itself [3] resembles this feature request.

1 - DDTSS - http://ddtp.debian.net/ddtss/
2 - http://www.isit.gl/l10n/ddtp-comment-field.jpeg
3 - https://bugs.launchpad.net/launchpad/+bug/25

- add generic group Users, which will have all privileges

summary: A way to group translation changes in fewer commits
description:
I wish it was possible for weblate to create fewer commits than one per msgstr change.

Our 9-year old project has about 11000 commits.  Our ".pot" file currently has 2647 messages.  That means that fully translating just 5 languages with weblate will create more commits than the entire rest of the project! (even more, since weblate will be creating commits on 'maint' and 'master' branches and then we'll double the length of the history when merging 'maint' into master!)

I don't know what the implementation would be like, but for example all changes by the same author without a pause longer than 15 minutes could be placed in a single commit.
